1:# BUILD-PLAN — six synthetic clients for challenge one
2:
3:Written 2026-08-21, second half of spike challenges/spike-002. Inputs: the
4:challenge text (`content/21-challenges/01-challenge-one.md`), the decisions in
5:`lab/NOTES.md`, the corpus map in `lab/FILE-MAP.md` **including the §7
6:correction pass** (ossola_ylenia re-synced; five reports rewritten; it is a
7:fifth N-400 packet, not a non-matter), the 25 runner reports in
8:`lab/reports/`, and the 9-sprint DS-260 masterkey prior art. Note on that
9:prior art: it was read in full before the ossola re-sync; the re-synced folder
10:(`7-sprint/` + `emails/`) no longer carries it on disk. Its schema is
11:summarised in FILE-MAP §3 and its adopt/reject rationale is §3 of this plan —
12:nothing in this plan depends on the deleted files.
13:
14:Everything in section 1 was **tested by execution during planning**, not
15:assumed. The riskiest unknown — whether the packet can be rendered at all with
16:the local toolchain — is already resolved.
17:
18:---
19:
20:## 0. THE TWO DECISIONS THAT SHAPE EVERYTHING ELSE
21:
22:### 0.1 The fork: perfect pairs or deliberate loss
23:
24:FILE-MAP's central finding is that the firm's real transcription is lossy
25:(malone: "Ma Lone", 10th St -> 16th St, vanished employers, vanished child).
26:Should the synthetic pairs reproduce that?
27:
28:**Decision: the pairs are internally perfect at the fact level. All mess lives
29:on the input side, and every piece of it has a deterministic resolution. No
30:transcription loss is seeded into any output.**
31:
32:Justification:
33:
34:1. *What the challenge tests.* The taker's plugin is judged by producing
35:   output "as close as possible" to the examples. If the examples carry
36:   errors, a diligent solver either reproduces errors as house style (teaching
37:   garbage-emulation) or notices input/output disagreement and cannot tell
38:   which side is authoritative. Either way the challenge stops being solvable
39:   by reasoning and starts being solvable only by luck. This is a Level 2
40:   course, not a forensics exam.
41:2. *What the firm's lossiness actually is.* It is a fact about a manual
42:   process. The plugin is supposed to beat the manual process — that is the
43:   course's point. An output that is the *correct* resolution of a messy input
44:   is the right target.
45:3. *Verification collapses without a clean invariant.* With perfect pairs the
46:   verifier asserts `output == f(resolved input)` with no carve-outs. With
47:   seeded errors, every future regeneration diff is ambiguous — "is this
48:   drift or a deliberate error?" — and the verifier needs a second ledger of
49:   intended wrongness. That doubles the machinery for negative teaching value.
50:4. *The instructive half of lossiness survives.* What made the malone finding
51:   valuable is cross-document disagreement. That is preserved — on the input
52:   side, where it belongs: a questionnaire answer superseded by a later email,
53:   a blank field filled by prose months later, a day trip that the firm's own
54:   instructions say to exclude. The output is the packet a careful firm would
55:   have filed. Chronological precedence (latest client statement wins) makes
56:   every disagreement resolvable, and the resolution is recorded in the
57:   masterkey.
58:
59:What we knowingly give up: a malone-style "audit the firm's transcription"
60:exercise. That is not what challenge one asks for. The same decision covers
61:the ossola correction's "soft inconsistencies to imitate" — three dates for
62:one filing, a continuous-residence computation short on its face. Those are
63:output-side inconsistencies, and they stay out for the same reasons the
64:transcription loss does: an output-side wrinkle either gets copied as house
65:style or poisons the `output == f(input)` invariant. Their input-side cousins
66:(a re-signature request months later, unexplained silence) remain available
67:as email texture in the input threads, where they cost nothing.
68:
69:**A second fork the correction pass surfaced: born-digital outputs or
70:simulated scans.** 54 of 185 corpus PDFs are image-only, including two of the
71:five filed N-400s (jacobs, ossola — printed, signed, scanned). **Decision:
72:every synthetic output is born-digital**, on the zhu model (the newest
73:generation, an AcroForm N-400 with a digital signature). Three reasons: the
74:challenge-taker's plugin can only ever produce born-digital output, so a
75:scanned worked example would set a target the plugin cannot match — "as close
76:as possible to the examples" must be achievable; a text-layered example keeps
77:a Level 2 challenge tractable (the taker's agents can pdftotext the worked
78:packets instead of reading 60 pages visually); and zhu is precedent that the
79:firm itself files born-digital. The scan-reading problem is still exercised —
80:on the *input* side, where phone photos of cards and notices belong to the
81:real problem being simulated.
82:
83:**The learnability rule that keeps the mess fair:** no mess type appears in a
84:test-client input unless the same mess type appears, with its resolution
85:demonstrated, in at least one worked pair. The bounded mess catalogue is in
86:section 5.3.
87:
88:### 0.2 The context problem: how one agent reviews cross-cutting artefacts
89:
90:A packet is cross-cutting — cover letter, TOC, N-400 and exhibits must agree
91:with each other and with the input — and six clients' documents do not fit in
92:one context. The answer here is architectural, in three parts, not a bigger
93:context window:
94:
95:1. **Facts flow forward through one small artefact.** Each client is fully
96:   described by a masterkey YAML (~300 lines, ~8 KB). Every generator — input
97:   fabricator, N-400 filler, cover-letter renderer — reads the masterkey, never
98:   another document. Consistency inside a client is therefore achieved **by
99:   construction**: two documents agree because they were rendered from the same
100:   key, not because someone checked them against each other afterwards.
101:2. **Mechanical work is scripts, not agents.** The N-400 fill, the cover
102:   letter, TOC, cover pages, the merge, the flatten — all deterministic
103:   renderers driven by the masterkey (toolchain proven, section 1). Agents do
104:   only the judgment work: casting, voice, email prose, review. What a script
105:   rendered from the key does not need an agent to re-derive.
106:3. **Verification flows backward, against extractions, never raw corpora.**
107:   Scripted verifiers re-extract facts from the *rendered* artefacts
108:   (pdftotext, pypdf field reads, docx reads) and diff them against the
109:   masterkey — cheap, exact, no context cost. Agent reviewers are reserved for
110:   what scripts cannot judge (plausibility, voice, look-and-feel), and the one
111:   *set-level* reviewer reads only compressed representations: six masterkeys
112:   + the registry + the per-client verifier reports (~60 KB total). No agent
113:   ever holds two clients' documents. The largest context anywhere in the plan
114:   is one client's full set (~50–150 KB of text), held by that client's own
115:   reviewer.
116:
117:A fourth rule serves both context and safety: **corpus quarantine.** Only the
118:Phase 1 style agent (and the scripted blocklist builder) touch `lab/` raw.
119:Every agent that writes synthetic content works from distilled artefacts
120:(STYLE-SPEC, templates, masterkeys, voice cards). This keeps generation
121:contexts small *and* makes leakage of real client facts structurally unlikely
122:rather than merely checked-for.
123:
124:---
125:
126:## 1. PHASE 0 — TOOLCHAIN SPIKE (already executed, 2026-08-21)
127:
128:Riskiest unknown first: can we produce a firm-grade packet locally? Yes.
129:Everything below was run and verified in this session.
130:
131:| step | tool | result |
132:|---|---|---|
133:| fetch blank N-400 | `curl https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/forms/n-400.pdf` | 200, 776 KB, edition 04/01/24, 14 pp — same edition as zhu's filed form |
134:| form anatomy | pypdf | 488 AcroForm fields under `form1[0]` (XFA hybrid). zhu's filed copy has XFA already stripped — precedent for our exact approach |

147:

150:blanks into the tools tree so the build is reproducible offline.

154:field map, including the travel-table row count that sets the addendum
155:threshold; (b) one visual pass over every filled page at pdftoppm resolution.
156:
157:---
158:
159:## 2. PHASE 1 — STYLE FREEZE
160:
161:*Consumes:* FILE-MAP §2 and §7, the actual packet files in
162:`jacobs_brent/Packet/` and `zhu_vivian/.../Tab A|Tab B/`, the exhibit-rule
163:corrections in `reports/ossola_ylenia--exhibit-origin.md`, the challenge
164:article's own promises.
165:*Produces:* `lab/synthetic/spec/STYLE-SPEC.md`, docx/YAML templates,
166:`lab/synthetic/tools/` skeleton, the corpus blocklist.
167:
168:*Topology:* **one agent**, corpus-exposed (the only content-side agent that
169:ever reads `lab/` raw). Style is a design act — FILE-MAP says so explicitly —
170:and parallelizing a design act produces incoherence. Standing instruction for
171:this agent, per the FILE-MAP §7 tooling correction: 54 of 185 corpus PDFs are
172:image-only (jacobs' filed N-400 among them) and their sidecars are stubs —
173:read scanned pages visually, and treat proper nouns lifted from scans as
174:unreliable. Plus one scripted job: build `blocklist.txt` (every proper noun,
175:number-string, address token from all corpus sidecars, with the §7 caveat
176:that scan-derived nouns get added in every OCR variant the reports recorded)
177:for Phase 6's leakage scan.
178:
179:The proposed resolution of the jacobs/zhu mix (the agent confirms details
180:against the raw files; the user signs off on taste):
181:
182:- **Structure: zhu.** TAB A (Summary) / TAB B (Biographical Information),
183:  applicant cover page with Classification Basis, DOCUMENT n dividers,
184:  everything merged into one flattened PDF. The challenge prompt promises
185:  cover pages, tabs and a merged PDF — that is zhu, and only zhu.
186:- **Wording: the shared modern core.** "TABLE OF CONTENTS" (both 2024 and
187:  2025 use it; "INDEX OF DOCUMENTS" died with the 2022 generation).
188:- **Cover letter: the recovered template** in FILE-MAP §2, jacobs-style Re:
189:  block with DOB line, eligibility clause + citation per basis
190:  (319 spousal: 8 U.S.C. § 1430(a), 8 C.F.R. § 319.1; 316: INA § 316(a),
191:  8 C.F.R. § 316.2), the fixed photocopies paragraph.
192:- **No G-1450, no G-1145.** The challenge article says the N-400 comes first
193:  among the documents; the izaguirre/ossola-generation openers (G-1145,
194:  G-1450 before the N-400) contradict that, and zhu's own TOC promised a
195:  G-1450 the packet did not contain. Fee travels as "the accompanying filing
196:  fee" in the cover letter ($760, current).
197:- **Packet order (fixed):** TAB A: 1 TOC, 2 Cover letter. TAB B: 3 N-400,
198:  4 passport bio page, 5 green card, 6 latest tax return, then conditional:
199:  7+ spousal passport bio / I-751 receipt / marriage evidence / travel
200:  addendum / court records. Continuous DOCUMENT numbering across tabs.
201:- **The exhibit rule, extended by the ossola correction.** FILE-MAP's
202:  `exhibits = f(basis, moral answers)` gains two arguments:
203:  `f(basis, moral answers, immigration history, supplied evidence)`.
204:  Conditional-resident history with the unconditional card not yet in hand
205:  drags in the I-751 receipt notice (I-797C) — ossola's new rule. A spousal
206:  basis binds in whatever bona fide marriage evidence the client actually
207:  supplied (joint deed, joint auto policy, child's passport, joint return) —
208:  the firm over-documents, and *which* documents appear is a function of what
209:  arrived, which is exactly the classification behaviour the plugin should be
210:  forced to exercise. STYLE-SPEC states the rule table; the Phase 5 verifier
211:  recomputes it per client.

## 6. PHASE 5 — VERIFICATION (four layers, cheapest first)

1. **Scripted intra-client locks** (`verify_client.py`, all six): re-extract
   from rendered artefacts and diff against the masterkey. N-400 field values
   (pypdf read of the unflattened component), TOC lines vs actual packet
   contents vs cover-page numbers, cover-letter facts, dates, A-numbers, MRZ
   checksums, exhibit set recomputed from the four-argument rule (basis,
   moral answers, immigration history, supplied evidence), filing-window
   arithmetic, merged-PDF page count == sum of components, merged text
   contains each component's fingerprint lines. Zero tolerance: any diff is a
   build bug.
2. **Per-client agent review, six in parallel.** Each holds ONE client's full
   set — extracted text of inputs and outputs plus the page images it asks
   for (~50–150 KB; comfortably one context). Hunts what locks cannot encode:
   timeline plausibility, narrative coherence between the emails and the
   form, voice consistency, whether the packet tells one story. Output: a
   discrepancy list referencing masterkey paths.
3. **Scripted set-level scans** (`verify_set.py`): leakage — every synthetic
   proper noun and digit-string grepped against the Phase 1 corpus blocklist,
   both directions, zero hits allowed; registry collisions; coverage matrix
   (both bases present, all three conditional exhibits exercised, six
   distinct voices, mess catalogue fully demonstrated-before-tested). Then
   **one set-reviewer agent** reads six masterkeys + registry + the six
   layer-2 reports — never a document — for the judgment call: does the set
   feel like six different clients of one firm.
4. **The dogfood test — the acceptance gate for the whole spike.** A clean
   solver context per test client: given only what a challenge-taker gets
   (the challenge article + three shipped worked pairs + that one test
   input), build the packet. Scripted fact-level diff of the solver's packet
   against the answer key. Pass bar: facts correct, structure correct,
   conditional exhibits correctly chosen; formatting is graded by eye, not
   byte. A solver failure caused by ambiguity is a **data bug** — fix the
   input surfaces, not the solver. Run for all three test clients; T2 first
   (the intended-median difficulty).

## 10. RISKS, UNCERTAINTIES, CUT ORDER

**Risks, ranked:**
1. *Unsolvable ambiguity from seeded mess.* Mitigated by the bounded
   catalogue, the demonstrated-before-tested rule, chronological precedence
   throughout, and the dogfood gate — the one test that measures the actual
   property the spike exists to deliver.
2. *Leakage of real client material.* Mitigated structurally (corpus
   quarantine: one exposed agent) and by the two-direction scripted blocklist
   scan; `lab/` added to install.sh strips.
3. *Field-map errors across 488 N-400 fields.* Mitigated by scripted
   round-trip (fill -> extract -> diff) and a one-time visual page pass. The
   04/01/24 edition's renumbered parts are an open detail — resolved by the
   field dump, Phase 3, before anything depends on it.
4. *Docx render fidelity.* Mitigated by the no-text-boxes template rule
   (the corpus's own converters proved the failure mode) and QA-on-images.
5. *Lockbox fact-check.* Real current N-400 paper-filing addresses need a
   web lookup (Phase 1). Fallback defined (§2).
6. *Document-image plausibility.* Phone-photo compositing might look toy.
   Acceptable floor: clean flat scans — the corpus contains both.

**Cut order if the spike runs short** (cut top-down):
1. Photo-realistic styling -> clean flat scans (keeps facts and modality).
2. The marriage-evidence cluster -> spousal clients carry spouse passport +
   I-797C only (drops the deed and policy renderers and two fabricated
   document types; the basis-driven exhibit rule stays learnable).
3. Dogfood three test clients -> dogfood T2 only.
4. The sixth voice register -> reuse a documented register, new nationality.
5. Email-thread depth (8–10 messages -> minimum 3 that carry the surfaces).
6. Answer-key rendering for T1/T3 (keep T2's for the dogfood diff).

**Never cut:** the masterkeys, the scripted lock verification, the leakage
scan, one dogfood run, the install.sh strip rule. Without any of those the
deliverable is either untrusted or unsafe to ship.

  `materials/challenge-one/` in this spike or a follow-up.

125	### 11.1 What the blocklist can and cannot see
126	
127	`build_blocklist.py` harvests every `.txt` sidecar, every email body, every
128	`.md` report and every path name under `lab/`. **54 of the 185 corpus PDFs are
129	image-only scans whose sidecars are the stub `[NO TEXT LAYER — …]`** (FILE-MAP
130	§7), and every identifier that lives *only* on a scan — jacobs' A-number, zhu's
131	police case number, the deed and tax preparers — is invisible to that pass.
132	
133	The script therefore runs a **second pass: `pdftoppm -r 200 -gray` plus
134	`tesseract` over each of the 54, cached by file hash in `tools/.ocr-cache/`**
135	so that reruns are offline and deterministic. OCR noise is *wanted* here: the
136	variant readings it produces are exactly the OCR variants FILE-MAP §7 says must
137	all go on the list ("Ma Lone" as well as "Malone"). Tokens read visually during
138	Phase 1 are additionally hardcoded in the script's `KEEP_ALWAYS`.

141	so the *cache* — not the OCR — is what makes the build reproducible; delete it
142	and the token list may shift slightly. And OCR on a photographed card or a
143	hand-annotated court form is imperfect, so **the leakage scan is necessary but

# SPEC-DELTA — Phase 2..6 reconciliation of the Phase-1 artefacts to STYLE-SPEC §16

Written at the head of the Phase 2–6 run. STYLE-SPEC §16 is the user's binding
ruling set and it postdates every other Phase-1 artefact on disk. The templates
and `tools/README.md` were written against §14 and therefore encoded overturned
law. A subagent handed those files would have implemented dead rules faithfully.
They are patched in place; this file is the ledger.

## A. Patched to §16

| file | was | now | authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `size_pt: 24` | `size_pt: 12` | §16 r3 |
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `green_card: GREEN CARD` | `PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD` | §16 r4 |
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `auto_policy: JOINT AUTOMOBILE POLICY` | `JOINT AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE POLICY` | §16 r4 precedent, decision D-A below |
| `templates/cover-page.yaml` | `A: SUMMARIES, B: BIOGRAPHICAL` | `A: SUMMARY, B: BIOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION` | §16 r2 |
| `templates/cover-letter.docx.yaml` | signature block `{FIRM_NAME}` / `By: {PREPARER_NAME}` / `Petition Preparer` | `Petition Preparer` alone; both slots deleted | §16 r7 |
| `tools/README.md` | `render_n400.py` fills Parts 11 **and 13**, renders Z003 signature | Part 11 only; Part 13 blank; unsigned; Z003 unused | §16 r10, r11 |
| `tools/README.md` | `build_blocklist.py` rerun instructions | DO NOT RERUN (OCR forbidden this run) | run order |

**Explicitly NOT changed:** tab cover pages stay at **24 pt**. §16 r3 lowers the
*dividers*; its own consequences note says so ("changes divider geometry").
Harmonising the tab covers down would be an unforced error.

## B. Decisions taken without asking

**D-A — the auto-policy title gains `INSURANCE`.** §4.3 set the divider
`JOINT AUTOMOBILE POLICY` while §4.4 set the TOC line `Joint automobile
insurance policy`. §16 "Still open" item 1 asks whether the invented
spousal-cluster titles read right and records that ruling 4 set a precedent —
the user preferred the formal name (`PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD`) over the
colloquial one (`GREEN CARD`). Applying that precedent: the divider takes the
fuller, formal string, the two strings stop disagreeing, and the component file
name follows. The other four invented titles (`SPOUSE'S PASSPORT`,
`FORM I-797C, NOTICE OF ACTION`, `JOINT DEED`, `CHILD'S PASSPORT`) were already
the formal form of their document and stand unchanged.

**D-B — the signature block keeps the role line.** §16 r7 forbids any firm or
preparer identity. It does not forbid the unattributed role, and STYLE-SPEC §11
lists both `Sincerely,` and `Petition Preparer` as strings the house style
requires every packet to contain. The block therefore closes:
`Sincerely,` · blank · blank · `Petition Preparer`. No name, no firm, no `By:`.

**D-C — `document-catalog.yaml` is the single join table.** Each document's file
name (§2.1), divider title (§4.3) and TOC line (§4.4) lived in three separate
prose tables. Renderers and `verify_client.py` now read one YAML instead of
three sections, so §4.4's TOC/divider/count lock cannot drift by transcription.

**D-D — `ships_as` rule confirmed** (§15.5, open): `authored_by: firm` ships
docx + pdf; forms and exhibits ship pdf only. This is the reading the run order
directs and it is now machine-readable in the catalog.

**D-E — the Part 13 assertion needs a positive control.** §13 D1 records that
the N-400 parts were renumbered between the 04/01/24 and 01/20/25 editions. A
verifier asserting "the Part 13 fields are empty" against field names that do
not exist on the committed blank passes vacuously while a filled preparer block
ships. `verify_client.py` must first PROVE the Part 11, Part 13 and signature
field names exist in the blank's 488-name dump, then assert Part 13 and the
signature fields are empty and Part 11 is populated.

**D-F — the leakage scan matches whole tokens, and §11 hits are not a halt.**
`blocklist.txt` carries 12,454 tokens including bare digit strings (`000000`,
`01212`, `02365`, `026300`). A naive substring grep over "every synthetic
digit-string" would hit on ZIPs, AGIs and dates and trip the run's halt
condition on noise. `verify_set.py` therefore matches on whole tokens with a
minimum length, and honours STYLE-SPEC §11's own rule: a hit on a §11-listed
house-style string is an exclusion-set bug to be recorded, not a halt. The halt
is reserved for a hit on a real corpus proper noun or identifier.

**D-G — `blocklist.txt` is consumed as built.** It and `.ocr-cache/` are
committed Phase-1 artefacts. The run order forbids OCR, so the script is not
re-run; the Phase-1 token list is authoritative for this build.

**D-H — §16 rulings 10 and 11 are honoured SEMANTICALLY, because the committed
blank has no Part 13.** Dumping all 488 fields of `blanks/n-400.pdf` with their
`/TU` tooltips shows the 01/20/25 edition's printed Parts do not match its
AcroForm field-name prefixes (the names still carry the previous edition's
`P12_`/`P13_`/`P14_`/`P15_`), and that **printed Part 13 has no fillable fields
at all**. §16 was written against zhu's 04/01/24 numbering. On the committed
blank the applicant's contact block is **printed Part 10** and the preparer
block is **printed Part 12**. The rulings are applied to the blocks the user
named by description, not by number: applicant phone/mobile/email FILLED,
preparer block EMPTY, applicant signature and its date EMPTY. Interpreter
(Part 11) and interview/oath signatures (Parts 15, 16) are also empty — no
interpreter is engaged, and 15/16 are executed at the USCIS interview.
The full field-name lists, and the positive control that stops the
"assert empty" check from passing vacuously, are in
`lab/synthetic/tools/n400-part-map.md`. Supporting dump:
`lab/synthetic/tools/n400-field-dump.tsv` (488 rows, page + type + tooltip).

# document-catalog.yaml — THE JOIN TABLE. Written in Phase 2, reconciled to
# STYLE-SPEC §16 (BINDING).
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every document carries three different strings living in
# three different STYLE-SPEC sections: the component FILE NAME (§2.1), the
# DIVIDER TITLE (§4.3) and the TOC LINE (§4.4). Three sources guarantee drift,
# and §4.4's lock exists precisely to catch it. Renderers and verify_client.py
# both read THIS file; neither re-derives a string from prose.
#
# RECONCILED AGAINST §16:
#   ruling 4  -> green-card divider is PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD, not GREEN CARD.
#   ruling 4 precedent (formal over colloquial), applied to the still-open
#             spousal-cluster titles of §16 "Still open" item 1:
#             auto policy gains INSURANCE, matching its own TOC line; the other
#             four spousal titles were already formal and stand unchanged.
#   ruling 11 -> the N-400 ships unsigned; nothing here renders a signature.
#
# ordering: `seq` is the append order. Core 1..6 are unconditional and fixed.
# Conditionals append in §9.2 precedence C1,C2,C3a,C3b,C3c,C4,C5,C6 and take the
# next DOCUMENT numbers. The DOCUMENT number IS the file-name number (§2).

pre_documents:      # no DOCUMENT number, no divider
  - id: applicant_cover_page
    file: "00. Applicant Cover Page"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    spec: "STYLE-SPEC §4.1"
  - id: tab_a_cover
    file: "Tab A (Content + Cover)/A-0. Tab Cover Page"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    strings: {line1: "TAB A", line2: "SUMMARY"}       # §16 ruling 2
    spec: "STYLE-SPEC §4.2 as amended by §16 ruling 2"
  - id: tab_b_cover
    file: "Tab B (Biographical Info)/B-0. Tab Cover Page"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    strings: {line1: "TAB B", line2: "BIOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION"}   # §16 ruling 2
    spec: "STYLE-SPEC §4.2 as amended by §16 ruling 2"

documents:
  # ---- TAB A, unconditional --------------------------------------------
  - id: table_of_contents
    seq: 1
    tab: A
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "Table of Contents"
    divider_title: "TABLE OF CONTENTS"
    toc_line: "Table of contents"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    renderer: render_docs.py

  - id: cover_letter
    seq: 2
    tab: A
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "Cover Letter"
    divider_title: "COVER LETTER"
    toc_line: "Cover letter"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    renderer: render_docs.py

  # ---- TAB B, unconditional --------------------------------------------
  - id: n400
    seq: 3
    tab: B
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "Form N-400, Application for Naturalization"
    divider_title: "FORM N-400"
    toc_line: "Form N-400, Application for Naturalization"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: form
    renderer: render_n400.py
    notes: "UNSIGNED (§16 r11). Part 13 blank (§16 r10). Part 11 filled."

  - id: applicant_passport
    seq: 4
    tab: B
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "Bio Page of Passport"
    divider_title: "PASSPORT"
    toc_line: "Bio page of latest passport of the applicant"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: fabricate_ids.py

  - id: green_card
    seq: 5
    tab: B
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "Permanent Resident Card"
    divider_title: "PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD"        # §16 ruling 4 (was GREEN CARD)
    toc_line: "Form I-551, Permanent Resident Card"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: fabricate_ids.py
    notes: "front and back"

  - id: tax_return
    seq: 6
    tab: B
    trigger: core
    file_stem: "{TAX_YEAR} Income Tax Return"
    divider_title: "{TAX_YEAR} INCOME TAX RETURN"
    toc_line: "Latest tax return"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: render_1040.py
    notes: "§9.3.1 — when the return is joint it IS the marriage evidence; never duplicated."

  # ---- TAB B, conditional, in §9.2 append precedence --------------------
  - id: spouse_passport
    trigger: C1
    condition: "basis == 319a"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Bio Page of Spouse Passport"
    divider_title: "SPOUSE'S PASSPORT"
    toc_line: "Bio page of latest passport of the applicant's spouse"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: fabricate_ids.py

  - id: i797c
    trigger: C2
    condition: "conditional_resident.was_cr AND unconditional I-551 not in hand at filing"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Form I-797C, Notice of Action"
    divider_title: "FORM I-797C, NOTICE OF ACTION"
    toc_line: "Form I-797C, Notice of Action"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: render_evidence.py

  - id: joint_deed
    trigger: C3a
    condition: "basis == 319a AND joint deed supplied"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Joint Deed"
    divider_title: "JOINT DEED"
    toc_line: "Joint deed"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: render_evidence.py

  - id: auto_policy
    trigger: C3b
    condition: "basis == 319a AND joint auto policy supplied"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Joint Automobile Insurance Policy"   # aligned to divider + TOC
    divider_title: "JOINT AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE POLICY"
    toc_line: "Joint automobile insurance policy"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: render_evidence.py

  - id: child_passport
    trigger: C3c
    condition: "basis == 319a AND child of the marriage exists AND child passport supplied"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Bio Page of Child Passport"
    divider_title: "CHILD'S PASSPORT"
    toc_line: "Bio page of latest passport of the applicant's child"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: fabricate_ids.py

  - id: travel_addendum
    trigger: C4
    condition: "countable trips exceed the Part 8 table rows OR any supplied trip was trimmed (day trip)"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Travel Addendum"
    divider_title: "TRAVEL ADDENDUM"
    toc_line: "Travel addendum"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    renderer: render_addendum.py

  - id: court_records
    trigger: C5
    condition: "any Part 9 arrest / citation / detention / charge answer is Yes"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Court Records"
    divider_title: "COURT RECORDS"
    toc_line: "Court records"
    ships: [pdf]
    authored_by: exhibit
    renderer: render_court_records.py

  - id: written_explanation
    trigger: C6
    condition: "any Part 9 Yes the form's own table cannot carry (removal, deportation, benefit denial)"
    tab: B
    file_stem: "Written Explanation"
    divider_title: "WRITTEN EXPLANATION"
    toc_line: "Written explanation"
    ships: [docx, pdf]
    authored_by: firm
    renderer: render_docs.py

# ships_rule (STYLE-SPEC §15.5, decided in Phase 2 without asking):
#   authored_by: firm    -> docx + pdf
#   authored_by: form    -> pdf only

quoted. Every line below is invented for this file.

four short messages in the whole thread.

## Daniel — texture

Native-speaker American English, fluent, organised, and far too long. He does
not just answer the question: he proposes a **process** for answering it. He
numbers his paragraphs. He anticipates the next three questions and answers
those too, sometimes wrongly. Sentences run **20 to 35 words**. He restates the
firm's question back before answering it, which doubles the length of every
message.

He is helpful in a way that occasionally creates work — he will summarise a
document rather than send it, then send it two messages later.

## Daniel — punctuation habits

Numbered lists (`1.`, `2.`, `3.`) inside otherwise ordinary prose. Bold-by-caps
for emphasis on a single word. Em dashes. He closes messages with a
forward-looking sentence: "Let me know what you need next and I'll get it
turned around tonight."

## Daniel — greeting and sign-off

Greeting: `Hi —` or `Following up on this:`. Sign-off: `Thanks, Daniel`.
Occasional "Sent from my phone, apologies for typos" that is followed by no
typos.

## Daniel — emotional temperature

Confident, mildly proprietorial about the matter, entirely well-meaning. He
treats the filing as a project he is managing. When something goes wrong — the
e-signature link — he does not complain; he routes around it and tells you what
he did.

## Daniel — being asked for something twice

He apologises briefly, then over-corrects: sends the thing, plus the two
adjacent things, plus an explanation of his filing system.

## Ha — texture

Short, careful, correct. Six to fifteen words. She writes only to fix a fact
Daniel has slightly wrong, and she is always right. Slight formality: `Thank
you.` as a complete message. No comma splices — her English is textbook-learnt

nothing in this plan depends on the deleted files.

Everything in section 1 was **tested by execution during planning**, not

---

## 0. THE TWO DECISIONS THAT SHAPE EVERYTHING ELSE

### 0.1 The fork: perfect pairs or deliberate loss

FILE-MAP's central finding is that the firm's real transcription is lossy
(malone: "Ma Lone", 10th St -> 16th St, vanished employers, vanished child).
Should the synthetic pairs reproduce that?

**Decision: the pairs are internally perfect at the fact level. All mess lives
on the input side, and every piece of it has a deterministic resolution. No
transcription loss is seeded into any output.**

Justification:

1. *What the challenge tests.* The taker's plugin is judged by producing
   output "as close as possible" to the examples. If the examples carry
   errors, a diligent solver either reproduces errors as house style (teaching
   garbage-emulation) or notices input/output disagreement and cannot tell
   which side is authoritative. Either way the challenge stops being solvable
   by reasoning and starts being solvable only by luck. This is a Level 2
   course, not a forensics exam.
2. *What the firm's lossiness actually is.* It is a fact about a manual
   process. The plugin is supposed to beat the manual process — that is the
   course's point. An output that is the *correct* resolution of a messy input
   is the right target.
3. *Verification collapses without a clean invariant.* With perfect pairs the
   verifier asserts `output == f(resolved input)` with no carve-outs. With
   seeded errors, every future regeneration diff is ambiguous — "is this
   drift or a deliberate error?" — and the verifier needs a second ledger of
   intended wrongness. That doubles the machinery for negative teaching value.
4. *The instructive half of lossiness survives.* What made the malone finding
   valuable is cross-document disagreement. That is preserved — on the input
   side, where it belongs: a questionnaire answer superseded by a later email,
   a blank field filled by prose months later, a day trip that the firm's own
   instructions say to exclude. The output is the packet a careful firm would
   have filed. Chronological precedence (latest client statement wins) makes
   every disagreement resolvable, and the resolution is recorded in the
   masterkey.

What we knowingly give up: a malone-style "audit the firm's transcription"
exercise. That is not what challenge one asks for. The same decision covers
the ossola correction's "soft inconsistencies to imitate" — three dates for
one filing, a continuous-residence computation short on its face. Those are
output-side inconsistencies, and they stay out for the same reasons the
transcription loss does: an output-side wrinkle either gets copied as house
style or poisons the `output == f(input)` invariant. Their input-side cousins
(a re-signature request months later, unexplained silence) remain available
as email texture in the input threads, where they cost nothing.

**A second fork the correction pass surfaced: born-digital outputs or
simulated scans.** 54 of 185 corpus PDFs are image-only, including two of the
five filed N-400s (jacobs, ossola — printed, signed, scanned). **Decision:
every synthetic output is born-digital**, on the zhu model (the newest
generation, an AcroForm N-400 with a digital signature). Three reasons: the
challenge-taker's plugin can only ever produce born-digital output, so a
scanned worked example would set a target the plugin cannot match — "as close
as possible to the examples" must be achievable; a text-layered example keeps
a Level 2 challenge tractable (the taker's agents can pdftotext the worked
packets instead of reading 60 pages visually); and zhu is precedent that the
firm itself files born-digital. The scan-reading problem is still exercised —
on the *input* side, where phone photos of cards and notices belong to the
real problem being simulated.

**The learnability rule that keeps the mess fair:** no mess type appears in a
test-client input unless the same mess type appears, with its resolution
demonstrated, in at least one worked pair. The bounded mess catalogue is in
section 5.3.

### 0.2 The context problem: how one agent reviews cross-cutting artefacts

A packet is cross-cutting — cover letter, TOC, N-400 and exhibits must agree
with each other and with the input — and six clients' documents do not fit in
one context. The answer here is architectural, in three parts, not a bigger
context window:

1. **Facts flow forward through one small artefact.** Each client is fully
   described by a masterkey YAML (~300 lines, ~8 KB). Every generator — input
   fabricator, N-400 filler, cover-letter renderer — reads the masterkey, never
   another document. Consistency inside a client is therefore achieved **by
   construction**: two documents agree because they were rendered from the same
   key, not because someone checked them against each other afterwards.
2. **Mechanical work is scripts, not agents.** The N-400 fill, the cover
   letter, TOC, cover pages, the merge, the flatten — all deterministic
   renderers driven by the masterkey (toolchain proven, section 1). Agents do
   only the judgment work: casting, voice, email prose, review. What a script
   rendered from the key does not need an agent to re-derive.
3. **Verification flows backward, against extractions, never raw corpora.**
   Scripted verifiers re-extract facts from the *rendered* artefacts
   (pdftotext, pypdf field reads, docx reads) and diff them against the
   masterkey — cheap, exact, no context cost. Agent reviewers are reserved for
   what scripts cannot judge (plausibility, voice, look-and-feel), and the one
   *set-level* reviewer reads only compressed representations: six masterkeys
   + the registry + the per-client verifier reports (~60 KB total). No agent
   ever holds two clients' documents. The largest context anywhere in the plan
   is one client's full set (~50–150 KB of text), held by that client's own
   reviewer.

A fourth rule serves both context and safety: **corpus quarantine.** Only the
Phase 1 style agent (and the scripted blocklist builder) touch `lab/` raw.
Every agent that writes synthetic content works from distilled artefacts
(STYLE-SPEC, templates, masterkeys, voice cards). This keeps generation
contexts small *and* makes leakage of real client facts structurally unlikely
rather than merely checked-for.

## 2. PHASE 1 — STYLE FREEZE

*Consumes:* FILE-MAP §2 and §7, the actual packet files in
`jacobs_brent/Packet/` and `zhu_vivian/.../Tab A|Tab B/`, the exhibit-rule
corrections in `reports/ossola_ylenia--exhibit-origin.md`, the challenge
article's own promises.
*Produces:* `lab/synthetic/spec/STYLE-SPEC.md`, docx/YAML templates,
`lab/synthetic/tools/` skeleton, the corpus blocklist.

*Topology:* **one agent**, corpus-exposed (the only content-side agent that
ever reads `lab/` raw). Style is a design act — FILE-MAP says so explicitly —
and parallelizing a design act produces incoherence. Standing instruction for
this agent, per the FILE-MAP §7 tooling correction: 54 of 185 corpus PDFs are
image-only (jacobs' filed N-400 among them) and their sidecars are stubs —
read scanned pages visually, and treat proper nouns lifted from scans as
unreliable. Plus one scripted job: build `blocklist.txt` (every proper noun,
number-string, address token from all corpus sidecars, with the §7 caveat
that scan-derived nouns get added in every OCR variant the reports recorded)
for Phase 6's leakage scan.

The proposed resolution of the jacobs/zhu mix (the agent confirms details
against the raw files; the user signs off on taste):

- **Structure: zhu.** TAB A (Summary) / TAB B (Biographical Information),
  applicant cover page with Classification Basis, DOCUMENT n dividers,
  everything merged into one flattened PDF. The challenge prompt promises
  cover pages, tabs and a merged PDF — that is zhu, and only zhu.
- **Wording: the shared modern core.** "TABLE OF CONTENTS" (both 2024 and
  2025 use it; "INDEX OF DOCUMENTS" died with the 2022 generation).
- **Cover letter: the recovered template** in FILE-MAP §2, jacobs-style Re:
  block with DOB line, eligibility clause + citation per basis
  (319 spousal: 8 U.S.C. § 1430(a), 8 C.F.R. § 319.1; 316: INA § 316(a),
  8 C.F.R. § 316.2), the fixed photocopies paragraph.
- **No G-1450, no G-1145.** The challenge article says the N-400 comes first
  among the documents; the izaguirre/ossola-generation openers (G-1145,
  G-1450 before the N-400) contradict that, and zhu's own TOC promised a
  G-1450 the packet did not contain. Fee travels as "the accompanying filing
  fee" in the cover letter ($760, current).
- **Packet order (fixed):** TAB A: 1 TOC, 2 Cover letter. TAB B: 3 N-400,
  4 passport bio page, 5 green card, 6 latest tax return, then conditional:
  7+ spousal passport bio / I-751 receipt / marriage evidence / travel
  addendum / court records. Continuous DOCUMENT numbering across tabs.
- **The exhibit rule, extended by the ossola correction.** FILE-MAP's
  `exhibits = f(basis, moral answers)` gains two arguments:
  `f(basis, moral answers, immigration history, supplied evidence)`.
  Conditional-resident history with the unconditional card not yet in hand
  drags in the I-751 receipt notice (I-797C) — ossola's new rule. A spousal
  basis binds in whatever bona fide marriage evidence the client actually
  supplied (joint deed, joint auto policy, child's passport, joint return) —
  the firm over-documents, and *which* documents appear is a function of what
  arrived, which is exactly the classification behaviour the plugin should be
  forced to exercise. STYLE-SPEC states the rule table; the Phase 5 verifier
  recomputes it per client.
- **Consciously rejected, with reasons recorded in STYLE-SPEC:** the ossola
  cover-letter variant (`Basis:` line replacing DOB/COB, no citation), the
  "Permanent Resident Since:" index header, the izaguirre "INDEX OF
  DOCUMENTS" heading — all pre-zhu generations the NOTES decision already
  excludes as format sources. Also rejected: the **supplemental cover letter**
  (ossola's mid-flight filing against a live case number). It is a real and
  interesting document type, but it is not a function of the input folder —
  it answers a later USCIS event — and the challenge command is
  `naturalize <input-folder>` producing one packet. It cannot be taught by
  input/output pairs and would only blur what an output folder is. If a
  future challenge level wants case-lifecycle work, it starts there.
- **Born-digital outputs only** (decision and reasons in §0.1): no simulated
  print-and-scan artefacts anywhere in an output folder.
- **Typography:** Times New Roman 12 throughout the firm-authored pages.
  Templates use plain paragraphs only — the corpus letterheads lived in docx
  text boxes and that is exactly what converters lose (jacobs' own signature
  block never extracted). Self-inflicted lesson: no text boxes.
- **Deliverable per output folder:** loose numbered components (docx + pdf,
  zhu's `A-1`, `B-4` prefix convention) *and* the flattened merged
  `N-400 Packet.pdf`. Teaches both layers.
- **The firm itself is invented.** SYMPLE, Marcel Oliveira, 26 Broadway and
  31 Hudson Yards are real reference facts and go on the blocklist. The
  registry (Phase 2) invents firm name, preparer name, letterhead address.
- **Lockbox:** needs a fact check the corpus cannot supply — current N-400
  paper-filing addresses by state (web lookup in this phase). Preference:
  choose the six states of residence so one lockbox serves all six clients.
  Fallback if the real mapping will not allow it: vary the lockbox *within
  the worked examples* so fact-dependence is learnable, never sprung on a
  test client first.
- **Timeline:** all six matters run Nov 2025 – Jul 2026 (in-world today is
  Aug 2026), so one form edition, one fee, one style generation — supporting
  the challenge's "the output does not look different" claim, which the real
  decade-spanning corpus cannot.

Barrier: user reviews STYLE-SPEC.md (taste sign-off) before anything renders.

## 3. PHASE 2 — CASTING: REGISTRY AND SIX MASTERKEYS

*Consumes:* this plan §7 (the profiles), STYLE-SPEC, the masterkey schema.
*Produces:* `lab/synthetic/registry.yaml`, six
`lab/synthetic/clients/<name>/masterkey.yaml`, six voice cards.

*Topology:*
1. **One casting agent** writes `registry.yaml` — the set-level namespace:
   firm identity; six names, A-numbers, DOBs, addresses, employers, phone
   numbers, emails; the coverage matrix (basis x mess x modality x voice);
   and six half-page briefs. Set-level design is single-brain work — coverage
   and collision-avoidance cannot be sharded. It also distils the six voice
   cards (verbatim register descriptions and *rewritten* sample lines — no
   corpus quotes cross the quarantine; the five documented registers in the
   reports are described, then re-voiced with invented content).
2. **Fan-out: six masterkey agents in parallel**, one per client. Context:
   its brief + the schema + STYLE-SPEC's "facts the output consumes" list.
   Output: one complete masterkey. No masterkey agent sees another client or
   the corpus.
3. **Barrier:** (a) scripted validation — schema check, registry collision
   check, derivation check (continuous-residence dates recompute from LPR

# SPEC-DELTA — Phase 2..6 reconciliation of the Phase-1 artefacts to STYLE-SPEC §16

Written at the head of the Phase 2–6 run. STYLE-SPEC §16 is the user's binding
ruling set and it postdates every other Phase-1 artefact on disk. The templates
and `tools/README.md` were written against §14 and therefore encoded overturned
law. A subagent handed those files would have implemented dead rules faithfully.
They are patched in place; this file is the ledger.

## A. Patched to §16

| file | was | now | authority |
|---|---|---|---|
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `size_pt: 24` | `size_pt: 12` | §16 r3 |
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `green_card: GREEN CARD` | `PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD` | §16 r4 |
| `templates/divider.yaml` | `auto_policy: JOINT AUTOMOBILE POLICY` | `JOINT AUTOMOBILE INSURANCE POLICY` | §16 r4 precedent, decision D-A below |
| `templates/cover-page.yaml` | `A: SUMMARIES, B: BIOGRAPHICAL` | `A: SUMMARY, B: BIOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION` | §16 r2 |
| `templates/cover-letter.docx.yaml` | signature block `{FIRM_NAME}` / `By: {PREPARER_NAME}` / `Petition Preparer` | `Petition Preparer` alone; both slots deleted | §16 r7 |
| `tools/README.md` | `render_n400.py` fills Parts 11 **and 13**, renders Z003 signature | Part 11 only; Part 13 blank; unsigned; Z003 unused | §16 r10, r11 |
| `tools/README.md` | `build_blocklist.py` rerun instructions | DO NOT RERUN (OCR forbidden this run) | run order |

**Explicitly NOT changed:** tab cover pages stay at **24 pt**. §16 r3 lowers the
*dividers*; its own consequences note says so ("changes divider geometry").
Harmonising the tab covers down would be an unforced error.

## B. Decisions taken without asking

**D-A — the auto-policy title gains `INSURANCE`.** §4.3 set the divider
`JOINT AUTOMOBILE POLICY` while §4.4 set the TOC line `Joint automobile
insurance policy`. §16 "Still open" item 1 asks whether the invented
spousal-cluster titles read right and records that ruling 4 set a precedent —
the user preferred the formal name (`PERMANENT RESIDENT CARD`) over the
colloquial one (`GREEN CARD`). Applying that precedent: the divider takes the
fuller, formal string, the two strings stop disagreeing, and the component file
name follows. The other four invented titles (`SPOUSE'S PASSPORT`,
`FORM I-797C, NOTICE OF ACTION`, `JOINT DEED`, `CHILD'S PASSPORT`) were already
the formal form of their document and stand unchanged.

**D-B — the signature block keeps the role line.** §16 r7 forbids any firm or
preparer identity. It does not forbid the unattributed role, and STYLE-SPEC §11
lists both `Sincerely,` and `Petition Preparer` as strings the house style
requires every packet to contain. The block therefore closes:
`Sincerely,` · blank · blank · `Petition Preparer`. No name, no firm, no `By:`.

**D-C — `document-catalog.yaml` is the single join table.** Each document's file
name (§2.1), divider title (§4.3) and TOC line (§4.4) lived in three separate
prose tables. Renderers and `verify_client.py` now read one YAML instead of
three sections, so §4.4's TOC/divider/count lock cannot drift by transcription.

**D-D — `ships_as` rule confirmed** (§15.5, open): `authored_by: firm` ships
docx + pdf; forms and exhibits ship pdf only. This is the reading the run order
directs and it is now machine-readable in the catalog.

**D-E — the Part 13 assertion needs a positive control.** §13 D1 records that
the N-400 parts were renumbered between the 04/01/24 and 01/20/25 editions. A
verifier asserting "the Part 13 fields are empty" against field names that do

signature fields are empty and Part 11 is populated.

**D-F — the leakage scan matches whole tokens, and §11 hits are not a halt.**
`blocklist.txt` carries 12,454 tokens including bare digit strings (`000000`,

digit-string" would hit on ZIPs, AGIs and dates and trip the run's halt

house-style string is an exclusion-set bug to be recorded, not a halt. The halt

# registry.yaml — the set-level namespace for the six synthetic N-400 packets.
# Phase 2a (CASTING). Authority chain, highest first:
#   1. spec/STYLE-SPEC.md §16   (the user's binding rulings)
#   2. spec/STYLE-SPEC.md       (the frozen house style)
#   3. spec/SPEC-DELTA.md       (D-A..D-G, already decided, not relitigated here)
#   4. templates/document-catalog.yaml  (the join table: file / divider / TOC line)
#   5. lab/BUILD-PLAN.md        (§3 schema, §5.3 mess catalogue, §7 profiles, §8 layout)
#
# NOTHING IN THIS FILE WAS READ FROM THE CORPUS. Phase 1 consumed lab/<client>/;
# this agent never opened it. Every proper noun, street, employer, telephone,
# e-mail address and identifier below is invented and was whole-token grepped
# against blocklist.txt (12,454 tokens) before it was written down.

build:
  phase: "2a — casting"
  produced:
    - "lab/synthetic/registry.yaml"
    - "lab/synthetic/clients/<slug>/brief.md   (x6)"
    - "lab/synthetic/clients/<slug>/voice-card.md (x6)"
  consumed:
    - "lab/synthetic/spec/STYLE-SPEC.md (§16 first, then whole)"
    - "lab/synthetic/spec/SPEC-DELTA.md"
    - "lab/synthetic/templates/document-catalog.yaml"
    - "lab/BUILD-PLAN.md §3, §5.3, §7, §8"
    - "lab/synthetic/blanks/n-400.pdf (field dump + text layer, no OCR)"
    - "lab/synthetic/blocklist.txt (leakage scan)"
  reconciliation_ledger: "lab/synthetic/spec/SPEC-DELTA.md"
  corpus_quarantine: "honoured — the five corpus matter folders under lab/ were not read, listed or opened. Phase 1 consumed them; STYLE-SPEC replaces them."
  in_world_window: "2025-11-01 .. 2026-07-31 (all six matters)"
  next_phase: "2b — six masterkey writers, one per client, each given ONLY its brief + the BUILD-PLAN §3 schema + STYLE-SPEC §12"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DECISIONS
# Every choice made without asking, with its reason. D1 is the one the run
# order names explicitly; the rest are this agent's.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
decisions:

  - id: D1
    title: "T2 Stavros's differentiator: C6, a written explanation, triggered by Part 9 Item 20"
    supersedes: "STYLE-SPEC §13 D13 and §16 'Still open' item 2"
    decision: >
      T2 Stavros stays on INA 316(a) and gains C6, a written explanation. Its
      conditional set becomes {C4 travel addendum, C6 written explanation} = 8
      documents, which is no longer W1 Almeida's {C4} = 7. The trigger is a
      Part 9 `Yes` that the form's own table cannot carry, and it is NOT an
      arrest, so C5 (court records) is NOT triggered.
    reason: >
      BUILD-PLAN §7 promises "no test client's exhibit set equals any worked
      example's", and as written T2 was W1 exactly: same basis, same single
      conditional, same seven documents — copyable, which is precisely what
      the plan says must fail. Four differentiators were available and three
      were rejected. (a) Spousal evidence (C1/C2/C3) is barred outright:
      STYLE-SPEC §9.3 rule 2, "316(a) admits no spousal evidence at all".
      (b) C5 court records would make T2 identical to T3 Adeyemi's {C4, C5}.
      (c) Moving T2 to 319(a) would cost T2 its ossola-register voice, its
      whole §5.3 mess catalogue and the plan's difficulty ramp. (d) C6 changes
      exactly one fact on the form and one document in the packet. C6 it is.
    form_binding_correction: >
      STYLE-SPEC §9.2 C6 names three example triggers — "removal proceedings,
      deportation, benefit denial". The committed blank was checked field by
      field and text layer by text layer: on edition 01/20/25 there is NO Part
      9 question asking whether an immigration benefit was ever denied. The
      non-tabulable hooks that do exist are Item 20, verbatim "Have you EVER
      been placed in removal, rescission, or deportation proceedings?", and
      Item 21, "Have you EVER been removed or deported from the United
      States?" (both route the applicant to Part 14. Additional Information,
      not to a table). T2's form hook is therefore ITEM 20 = Yes; the denied
      benefit survives as the NARRATIVE the written explanation carries — a
      2013 I-130/I-485 filed by his U.S. citizen daughter, the I-485 denied
      2015-02-11, an NTA issued 2015-09-14, proceedings terminated 2018-11-06,
      lawful permanent residence granted 2020-01-23. This keeps the spirit of
      the instruction (an immigration-history denial, not an arrest, so no C5)
      while binding to a field that exists. Stated loudly rather than diverged
      from silently.
    consequence_for_w3: >
      W3 Nowak must demonstrate C6 independently of C5 or T2's C6-without-C5
      is unlearnable. W3 therefore carries BOTH an arrest (Part 9 Item 15.b =
      Yes, disorderly conduct 2019-11-08, dismissed 2020-02-14 → C5) AND a
      separate, unrelated Item 20 = Yes (removal proceedings 2015-03-11,
      terminated 2017-09-22 → C6). The resulting truth table is fully
      separable across the six clients and is set out in
      coverage_matrix.moral_character_truth_table.

  - id: D2
    title: "BUILD-PLAN §8's T1 slug is renamed `tran_daniel`"
    supersedes: "BUILD-PLAN §8's shipped folder name for T1 (the original is not reproduced here — see the leakage note)"
    decision: "T1's correspondent is Daniel Quang Tran; the shipped folder is `tran_daniel/`."
    reason: >
      The given name in BUILD-PLAN §8's original slug is on blocklist.txt as
      a whole token (1 occurrence). It is a real corpus proper noun that this
      agent cannot inspect (quarantine), and RUN-PHASE-2-6.md makes any
      leakage hit a halt condition. A folder name ships, so the token would
      ship. BUILD-PLAN §7 states its own facts are "placeholders for the
      registry to finalise", which is the authority to change it; `Daniel`
      returns zero hits and `Tran` returns zero hits. Phase 6 must land
      `tran_daniel/`, not the original path. Fifteen common given names were
      tested against the blocklist and NINE of them are on it, so given-name
      choice is a leakage decision throughout this registry and not a taste
      one. (The nine are not spelled out here: this file is scanned too, and a
      registry that documents a blocklisted token by quoting it trips the very
      halt it is explaining. Re-derive them by running the check.)

  - id: D3
    title: "Three folders are correspondent-named, not two"
    decision: >
      `kavanagh_liam` (applicant is his wife, Siobhan Brennan), `tran_daniel`
      (applicant is his wife, Vu Thanh Ha) and `stavros_daphne` (applicant is
      her father, Konstantinos Stavros).
    reason: >
      BUILD-PLAN §8 marks two folders correspondent-named; §5.3's mess table
      lists the mess type as W2-demonstrated, T1-reused. But §7 describes T2's
      register as "Greek-American", and an applicant for naturalization cannot
      be American. The plain reading is that T2's correspondent is the
      American member of a Greek household — the daughter — and the applicant
      is her father. The third instance is recorded explicitly in
      coverage_matrix.mess_types so nobody mistakes it for an unlisted mess.
    mitigation: >
      T2 is the median difficulty and BUILD-PLAN §6 layer 4 dogfoods it first,
      and it now carries five mess types. The folder-name indirection must
      therefore be SIGNPOSTED, not puzzled: Daphne names her father in full in
      the first e-mail of the thread, signs every message as his daughter, and
      never refers to the applicant as "me". Written into her brief and her
      voice card.

  - id: D4
    title: "Six firm-identity fact slots in STYLE-SPEC §12.9 are DELETED, not filled"
    decision: >
      firm name · preparer name · preparer daytime telephone · preparer e-mail ·
      preparer business address · and §13 D4's sentence "The registry still
      invents a firm address — Phase 3 needs it for the N-400's Part 13
      preparer block" are all DEAD. The registry invents none of them. Only
      `preparer_title` survives, unattributed.
    reason: >
      §16 ruling 7 forbids a firm identity anywhere in any artefact and §16
      ruling 10 empties the Part 13 preparer block, which was the only
      remaining consumer of a business address. §12.9 and §13 D4 were written
      before those rulings and were not rewritten. A masterkey writer reading
      §12.9 as a checklist would dutifully invent all five. They are named
      here as deleted so that does not happen. Per SPEC-DELTA D-B the
      signature block closes `Sincerely,` · blank · blank · `Petition
      Preparer` — the role line with no name and no `By:`.

  - id: D5
    title: "Lockbox and carrier assignment: two lockboxes, both carriers, every test combination demonstrated first"
    decision: >
      Elgin+USPS (W1 Almeida → T2 Stavros) · Chicago+FEDERAL EXPRESS
      (W2 Kavanagh → T1 Tran) · Chicago+USPS (W3 Nowak → T3 Adeyemi).
    reason: >
      §16 ruling 9 (UPHELD) requires at least two lockboxes and both carriers,
      each demonstrated in a worked pair before a test client needs it. Three
      worked pairs give at most three (lockbox, carrier) pairs, so the three
      test clients must reuse exactly those three — which is what this does,
      one-to-one. States were then chosen to fit: MA and NJ route to Elgin;
      IL, MI, OH and WI route to Chicago (STYLE-SPEC §7). The lockbox is a
      function of the CURRENT address, and two clients (W2, T2) carry a
      superseded-address mess, so both moves were kept INSIDE one state —
      a cross-state move would make the lockbox itself ambiguous and turn a
      bounded mess into an unbounded one.

  - id: D6
    title: "Tax years split 4/2 across the two committed blanks, and BOTH branches are demonstrated in a worked pair"
    decision: "W1 TY2024 · W2 TY2024 · W3 TY2025 (worked) — T2 TY2024 · T1 TY2025 · T3 TY2025 (test)."
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §13 D11: filed before ~mid-April 2026 → TY2024
      (`f1040--2024.pdf`); filed after → TY2025 (`f1040.pdf`). The obvious
      casting — worked pairs early in the window, test clients late — would
      have put all three worked pairs on TY2024 and all three test clients on
      TY2025, so the TY2025 branch would be TESTED WITHOUT EVER BEING
      DEMONSTRATED and a solver copying the worked pairs would file a 2024
      return in June 2026. W3's filing date was therefore moved to 2026-05-26
      so a worked pair carries TY2025, and T2's to 2026-03-17 so a test client
      carries TY2024. The worked/test split is not chronological; nothing
      requires it to be.

  - id: D7
    title: "The day trip appears on NEITHER the Part 8 table NOR the travel addendum"
    decision: >
      A day trip (entire trip completed within 24 hours) is listed by the
      client on the input side, is trimmed from the N-400 Part 8 table, and is
      ALSO absent from the travel addendum. C4 fires for W1 and T2 on the
      row-count disjunct, never on the trimmed-day-trip disjunct.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §4.5 fixes the addendum's opening sentence verbatim, and it
      says "excluding day trips"; the blank's own Part 8 instruction says "Do
      not include day trips (where the entire trip was completed within 24
      hours) in the table". STYLE-SPEC §9.2's C4 condition offers a second
      disjunct — "any supplied trip was trimmed from the form (day trips)" —
      which cannot be live at the same time: a trip the addendum excludes by
      its own wording cannot be the reason the addendum exists. Both W1 and T2
      independently exceed the table's row count, so the rule is never load
      bearing for them; it is settled here so that a masterkey writer does not
      put the day trip in the addendum, where Phase 5's "addendum ⊇ Part 8"
      lock would happily pass over a wrong fact.
    verified_fact: >
      The Part 8 table on the committed 01/20/25 blank has EXACTLY SIX ROWS —
      fields P8_Line1_DateLeft1..6 / P8_Line1_DateReturn1..6 /
      P8_Line1_Countries2..6, on page 6 of 14 (page index 5). Row 1's country
      field is misnamed `P9_Line1_Countries1[0]` by the form vendor; it sits
      in the same subform as the Part 8 fields and IS the Part 8 row-1 country
      field. Phase 3's fieldmap_n400.yaml must not be fooled by the name.
      STYLE-SPEC §8's "6 rows on that edition" was written about zhu's OLDER
      04/01/24 form; it happens to be right for 01/20/25 too, and is now
      confirmed against the blank rather than inherited.
    addendum_page_reference: "Page 6 — the value STYLE-SPEC §4.5's `Page {p}, Part 8, Question 1` slot takes for all six clients."

  - id: D8
    title: "Every telephone number is in the 555-01xx fiction block; e-mail domains are invented"
    decision: >
      All telephone numbers use a real area code for the client's region plus
      the reserved fictional exchange 555-0100..555-0199. Personal e-mail runs
      on two invented consumer domains, `quillmail.com` and `brightpost.net`;
      work e-mail runs on the invented employer domains.
    reason: >
      Real free-mail domains cannot be used: the three commonest consumer
      mail domains are all on blocklist.txt as whole tokens (the corpus is
      full of them), so a synthetic packet carrying one would trip the Phase 5
      layer-3 halt. STYLE-SPEC §11 does not list them as shared house-style
      strings, so they would not be excused either. Invented domains cost
      nothing and scan clean. The 555-01xx block is the equivalent move for
      telephone numbers. Again the offending tokens are not quoted here — see
      decision D2's closing note.

  - id: D9
    title: "All names are rendered ASCII-only"
    decision: >
      `Siobhan`, not `Siobhán`. `Vu Thanh Ha`, not `Vũ Thanh Hà`.
      `Konstantinos`, not `Κωνσταντίνος`.
    reason: >
      The names travel through pypdf AcroForm values, a passport MRZ (which is
      A-Z, 0-9 and `<` only, with its own transliteration rules), Times New
      Roman docx runs and a `soffice --headless` conversion. Diacritics
      survive some of that and not all of it, and a mismatch between the MRZ
      transliteration and the printed name would break STYLE-SPEC §9.4's name
      lock for a reason that has nothing to do with the rule being taught.
      The input side may still show a client typing an accented name in prose;
      the packet is ASCII.

  - id: D10
    title: "T1's marriage predates her permanent residence by more than two years"
    decision: "Married 2020-03-14; LPR 2022-11-30; class of admission IR6; conditional_resident.was_cr = false."
    reason: >
      Had T1 become a permanent resident within two years of the marriage she
      would have been admitted as a CONDITIONAL resident (CR6) under INA 216,
      which produces an I-751 and puts C2 (Form I-797C) in play. Her mandated
      set is {C1, C3a, C3c, C4} = 10 documents, and a stray C2 would both
      break the target matrix and collapse her story into W2's — W2's
      conditional-residence history is W2's whole differentiator. Two years
      and eight months keeps her unconditional. Every client's
      `class_of_admission` is stated explicitly for the same reason: the green
      card exhibit prints the category and STYLE-SPEC §9.4 locks it.
      W2 is the ONLY conditional resident in the set (CR6, married 2022-02-19,
      resident 2022-09-15 — seven months, correctly conditional).

  - id: D11
    title: "Two clients carry family facts that trigger nothing"
    decision: >
      W3 Nowak is divorced and has a son; T3 Adeyemi is married to a
      non-citizen and has a daughter. Neither produces a single conditional
      document.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §9.3 rule 2 ("316(a) admits no spousal evidence at all") and
      §9.2 C3c (which requires `basis == 319(a)` AND a child AND a supplied
      passport) are both easy to mis-learn as "a spouse means a spouse's
      passport" and "a child means a child's passport". Two negative controls
      make the rule visible: T3 has a living spouse and no C1, W3 has a child
      and no C3c. Both are worked-or-tested against W2 and T1, where the same
      facts DO produce documents because the basis is 319(a). This costs two
      lines of masterkey and buys the rule its contrapositive.

  - id: D12
    title: "Both 319(a) clients file jointly, and DOCUMENT 6 absorbs the joint return"
    decision: "W2 and T1 file Married Filing Jointly; the joint return is DOCUMENT 6 and appears once."
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §16 ruling 13 and §9.3 rule 1. Stated at casting time because
      a masterkey writer with a joint return and a marriage-evidence cluster
      in front of them is one step from listing it twice, which would break
      the §4.4 lock (TOC line count == divider count == DOCUMENT count).

  - id: D13
    title: "T1's requested new name appears in exactly one place"
    decision: >
      Vu Thanh Ha requests the name `Ha Thanh Tran` on the N-400. That string
      appears ONLY in the Part 2 name-change item. The applicant cover page,
      the cover letter Re: block, the passport and its MRZ, the green card,
      the tax return and every other artefact carry the CURRENT legal name,
      `Vu Thanh Ha`.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §9.4 locks surname and given name identical across the N-400,
      the passport MRZ and the cover letter. A requested name is a request,
      not a fact about any document that exists at filing. This is the single
      most likely fact error in the whole set and is repeated at the head of
      T1's brief.

  - id: D14
    title: "Nationality adjectives and their articles are frozen here, not derived downstream"
    decision: >
      "a Brazilian national" · "an Irish national" · "a Polish national" ·
      "a Vietnamese national" · "a Greek national" · "a Nigerian national".
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §5's cover-letter template carries an `{A|AN}` slot next to a
      `{NATIONALITY ADJECTIVE}` slot. A renderer choosing the article from the
      first letter gets `an Irish` right and nothing else wrong here, but the
      rule is not "vowel letter" (it is vowel SOUND), so the article is stored
      as data alongside the adjective and never computed.

  - id: D15
    title: "Selective Service is No for every applicant, by construction"
    decision: >
      All three male applicants (W1 Almeida, T2 Stavros, T3 Adeyemi) first
      lived in the United States after their 26th birthday, so Part 9 Item
      22.a is No and 22.b/22.c do not arise.
    reason: >
      A `No` at 22.b is a real-world written-explanation trigger and would be
      a FOURTH C6 pathway competing with Item 20 — it would muddy the C5/C6
      truth table the set exists to teach. Arrival dates were cast to close
      it: Almeida first entered 2015 at 27, Adeyemi 2016 at 30, Stavros 2011
      at 54.

  - id: D16
    title: "Engagement dates run 5 to 9 weeks before filing"
    decision: "Each matter opens 5–9 weeks before it is filed; the input e-mail threads live in that window."
    reason: >
      Phase 4 writes threads dated between the engagement date and the filing
      date, and messes like 'password in a later e-mail', 'superseded address'
      and 'blank field supplied later by prose' need enough room for a
      chronology to exist. Under a fortnight there is no room; over three
      months the thread stops reading like one matter. Five to nine weeks also
      keeps every thread inside the 2025-11 .. 2026-07 in-world window.

## 9. THE EXHIBIT RULE — a four-argument decision table

`exhibits = f(basis, moral-character answers, immigration history, supplied
evidence)`

FILE-MAP §3 had two arguments; ossola/exhibits and ossola/provenance add the
third and fourth. The Phase 5 verifier recomputes this table per client and
diffs it against the rendered packet.

### 9.1 Unconditional core — every packet, every client

| DOC | document | why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Table of contents | firm-authored |
| 2 | Cover letter | firm-authored |
| 3 | Form N-400 | the application |
| 4 | Applicant's passport bio page | identity; supplies name, DOB, COB, MRZ |
| 5 | Form I-551, Permanent Resident Card (front and back) | supplies A-number and LPR date |
| 6 | Latest tax return | continuous-residence and good-moral-character evidence |

Attested as the invariant core across all five corpus matters (FILE-MAP §2
"The invariant core"; ossola/exhibits "ALWAYS"). The tax return is core in
zhu and ossola and is kept core here (taste call 5) even though jacobs' 2025
packet has only four documents — jacobs is a returning client whose packet is
the thinnest in the corpus.

### 9.2 Conditional documents, in append precedence order

| order | document | argument | trigger — exact condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Spouse's passport bio page | **basis** | `basis == 319(a)` |
| C2 | Form I-797C, Notice of Action | **immigration history** | `conditional_resident.was_cr == true` **and** the unconditional I-551 was not in hand at the filing date (I-751 pending, or approved so late that the card post-dates filing) |
| C3a | Joint deed | **supplied evidence** | `basis == 319(a)` **and** a joint deed is among the documents the client supplied |
| C3b | Joint automobile insurance policy | **supplied evidence** | `basis == 319(a)` **and** supplied |
| C3c | Child's passport bio page | **supplied evidence** | `basis == 319(a)` **and** a child of the marriage exists **and** the child's passport was supplied |
| C4 | Travel addendum | **derived** | trips within the residence window exceed the Part 8 table's row count, **or** any supplied trip was trimmed from the form (day trips) |
| C5 | Court records | **moral-character answers** | any Part 9 arrest / citation / detention / charge answer is `Yes` |
| C6 | Written explanation | **moral-character answers** | any Part 9 `Yes` that the form's own table cannot carry (removal proceedings, deportation, benefit denial) |

### 9.3 Rules that fall out of the table

1. **A joint tax return is not a separate document.** If the applicant files
   jointly, DOCUMENT 6 (the core tax return) *is* the marriage evidence.
   Ossola's packet listed `9. Tax Returns` inside the marriage cluster; here
   the core slot absorbs it. Taste call 13.
2. **316(a) admits no spousal evidence at all** — no C1, no C2, no C3. FILE-MAP
   §3: "INA 316 five-year → no spousal evidence at all."
3. **The firm over-documents, but only what arrived.** C3a–C3c are a function
   of *supplied* evidence, not of the basis alone. This is the classification
   behaviour the plugin must exercise (BUILD-PLAN §2).
4. **Every conditional document is traceable to a fact on the form.** If a
   packet contains a document that no row above triggers, the packet is wrong.
   FILE-MAP §3: "Everything beyond the invariant core is conditional, and the
   condition is always traceable to a form answer."
5. **The travel addendum is a superset of the form's travel table** — the
   addendum lists every countable trip; the form lists as many as fit.
6. **G-1450 and G-1145 are never triggered** (§10).

### 9.4 Cross-document consistency locks (carried from FILE-MAP §3)

Surname and given name identical on N-400, passport MRZ and cover letter · DOB
identical everywhere it appears (cover page, cover letter, N-400, passport,
green card) · place of birth identical on N-400 and passport · A-number

## 12. FACTS THE OUTPUT CONSUMES

Every distinct fact some output artefact needs. Phase 2's masterkey schema is
validated against this list; a fact here with no masterkey home is a schema
bug, and a fact here with no input surface is a broken test client
(BUILD-PLAN §3). Benchmarked against ossola/provenance, which maps one real
packet field by field.

### 12.1 Identity
family name · given name · middle name · other names used since birth (0–2,
family/given/middle each) · name-change requested? and if so the new
family/given/middle name · honorific (`Mr.`/`Ms.`) · pronouns (subject,
possessive) · date of birth · sex · country of birth · country of citizenship
or nationality · nationality adjective (for the cover letter's "an Australian
national") · SSN · USCIS online account number (or none) · height (feet,
inches) · weight (pounds, 3 digits) · eye colour · hair colour · ethnicity
(Hispanic/Not Hispanic) · race (one or more)

### 12.2 Contact
daytime telephone · mobile telephone · email address

### 12.3 Immigration status
A-number (9 digits) · date became a permanent resident (LPR date) · class of
admission · eligibility basis (`316(a)` / `319(a)`) · classification-basis
string for the cover page · was a conditional resident? · I-751 receipt
number · I-751 received date · I-751 notice dates · I-751 status at filing ·
unconditional card in hand at filing? · **derived:** earliest filing date
(LPR + 3y − 90d, or LPR + 5y − 90d) · continuous-residence years at filing

### 12.4 Residence
current physical address (street number and name, unit type + number, city,
state, ZIP, country, from-date) · mailing address if different · prior
addresses, gap-free, covering the residence window (street, unit, city, state,
ZIP, country, from, to) · state of residence → lockbox (§7)

### 12.5 Marital and family
marital status · number of times married · date of current marriage · spouse
family/given/middle name · spouse DOB · spouse A-number (if any) · spouse is a
U.S. citizen? · citizen at birth or naturalised (+ date and place if
naturalised) · spouse's address (same as applicant?) · spouse's employer ·
spouse's number of prior marriages · prior marriages of the applicant (name,
dates, how ended) · each child: family/given/middle name, DOB, country of
birth, relationship type, address, lives with applicant? · each parent: name,
U.S. citizen?, married before the applicant turned 18?

### 12.6 Employment and education
per entry, covering the residence window: employer or school name · city ·
state · ZIP · country · occupation or field of study · from date · to date ·
"present" flag

### 12.7 Travel
per trip: departure date · return date · country or countries · day count ·
`on_form` flag · `why_excluded` (day trip / outside window) · **derived:**
total days outside the U.S. · whether an addendum is triggered (§9.2 C4)

### 12.8 Moral character
every Part 9 item: answer (`Yes`/`No`) and, where `Yes`, the explanation text,
the arrest/charge detail row (date, place, offence, outcome), and whether it
triggers court records (C5) or a written explanation (C6) · Part 10 fee
reduction (`No`) · Part 12 oath answers (bear arms / noncombatant service /
work of national importance / support the Constitution / no mental
reservation)

### 12.9 Matter and firm
firm name · preparer name · preparer title (`Petition Preparer`) · preparer
daytime telephone · preparer email · preparer business address (street, city,
state, ZIP) · engagement date · **filing date** (drives the cover-letter date
and the signature date) · carrier (`U.S. POSTAL SERVICE (USPS)` /
`FEDERAL EXPRESS`) · lockbox block (derived, §7) · fee (`760.00`) · form
edition string (`01/20/25`)

### 12.10 Exhibit facts
- **applicant passport:** issuing country · passport number · surname and given
  names as printed · nationality · DOB · sex · place of birth · issue date ·
  expiry date · issuing authority · MRZ line 1 and line 2 (check digits
  computed)
- **green card (I-551):** surname · given name · A-number (`USCIS#`) ·
  category / class of admission · country of birth · DOB · sex · card expiry ·
  `Resident Since` date · front and back
- **spouse's passport / child's passport:** the same field set
- **tax return:** tax year · filing status · taxpayer and spouse names and
  SSNs · address as printed · wages · adjusted gross income · total tax ·
  refund or amount owed · preparer name · which blank (`f1040.pdf` = TY2025,
  `f1040--2024.pdf` = TY2024; §13 D11)
- **Form I-797C:** receipt number · case type (`I751`) · received date ·
  notice date · notice type · applicant name · A-number · fee paid
- **joint deed:** grantor(s) · grantee(s) · property address · county ·
  recording date · instrument number · consideration · preparer
- **joint automobile policy:** insurer · policy number · named insureds ·
  policy period (effective, expiry) · garaging address · vehicle(s) · coverages
- **court records:** court name and location · police case number · docket
  number · charge(s) with statute number and offence date · plea · disposition
  and disposition date · judge · clerk certification date and seal
- **travel addendum:** the full trip list (§4.5) · residence window (3 or 5
  years) · the Part 8 page number on the filled form
- **resume** (input-side, but locked to Part 7): employer, title, city, dates

### 12.11 Facts that exist only in the output
TOC line list (derived from §9) · DOCUMENT count · each DOCUMENT's divider
title (§4.3) and TOC line (§4.4) · per-component page count · merged page count
· eligibility clause and citation (§5.1) · nationality adjective (§12.1)
