content.content:
- id: D5
    title: "Lockbox and carrier assignment: two lockboxes, both carriers, every test combination demonstrated first"
    decision: >
      Elgin+USPS (W1 Almeida → T2 Stavros) · Chicago+FEDERAL EXPRESS
      (W2 Kavanagh → T1 Tran) · Chicago+USPS (W3 Nowak → T3 Adeyemi).
    reason: >
      §16 ruling 9 (UPHELD) requires at least two lockboxes and both carriers,
      each demonstrated in a worked pair before a test client needs it. Three
      worked pairs give at most three (lockbox, carrier) pairs, so the three
      test clients must reuse exactly those three — which is what this does,
      one-to-one. States were then chosen to fit: MA and NJ route to Elgin;
      IL, MI, OH and WI route to Chicago (STYLE-SPEC §7). The lockbox is a
      function of the CURRENT address, and two clients (W2, T2) carry a
      superseded-address mess, so both moves were kept INSIDE one state —
      a cross-state move would make the lockbox itself ambiguous and turn a
      bounded mess into an unbounded one.

  - id: D6
    title: "Tax years split 4/2 across the two committed blanks, and BOTH branches are demonstrated in a worked pair"
    decision: "W1 TY2024 · W2 TY2024 · W3 TY2025 (worked) — T2 TY2024 · T1 TY2025 · T3 TY2025 (test)."
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §13 D11: filed before ~mid-April 2026 → TY2024
      (`f1040--2024.pdf`); filed after → TY2025 (`f1040.pdf`). The obvious
      casting — worked pairs early in the window, test clients late — would
      have put all three worked pairs on TY2024 and all three test clients on
      TY2025, so the TY2025 branch would be TESTED WITHOUT EVER BEING
      DEMONSTRATED and a solver copying the worked pairs would file a 2024
      return in June 2026. W3's filing date was therefore moved to 2026-05-26
      so a worked pair carries TY2025, and T2's to 2026-03-17 so a test client
      carries TY2024. The worked/test split is not chronological; nothing
      requires it to be.

  - id: D7
    title: "The day trip appears on NEITHER the Part 8 table NOR the travel addendum"
    decision: >
      A day trip (entire trip completed within 24 hours) is listed by the
      client on the input side, is trimmed from the N-400 Part 8 table, and is
      ALSO absent from the travel addendum. C4 fires for W1 and T2 on the
      row-count disjunct, never on the trimmed-day-trip disjunct.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §4.5 fixes the addendum's opening sentence verbatim, and it
      says "excluding day trips"; the blank's own Part 8 instruction says "Do
      not include day trips (where the entire trip was completed within 24
      hours) in the table". STYLE-SPEC §9.2's C4 condition offers a second
      disjunct — "any supplied trip was trimmed from the form (day trips)" —
      which cannot be live at the same time: a trip the addendum excludes by
      its own wording cannot be the reason the addendum exists. Both W1 and T2
      independently exceed the table's row count, so the rule is never load
      bearing for them; it is settled here so that a masterkey writer does not
      put the day trip in the addendum, where Phase 5's "addendum ⊇ Part 8"
      lock would happily pass over a wrong fact.
    verified_fact: >
      The Part 8 table on the committed 01/20/25 blank has EXACTLY SIX ROWS —
      fields P8_Line1_DateLeft1..6 / P8_Line1_DateReturn1..6 /
      P8_Line1_Countries2..6, on page 6 of 14 (page index 5). Row 1's country
      field is misnamed `P9_Line1_Countries1[0]` by the form vendor; it sits
      in the same subform as the Part 8 fields and IS the Part 8 row-1 country
      field. Phase 3's fieldmap_n400.yaml must not be fooled by the name.
      STYLE-SPEC §8's "6 rows on that edition" was written about zhu's OLDER
      04/01/24 form; it happens to be right for 01/20/25 too, and is now
      confirmed against the blank rather than inherited.
    addendum_page_reference: "Page 6 — the value STYLE-SPEC §4.5's `Page {p}, Part 8, Question 1` slot takes for all six clients."

  - id: D8
    title: "Every telephone number is in the 555-01xx fiction block; e-mail domains are invented"
    decision: >
      All telephone numbers use a real area code for the client's region plus
      the reserved fictional exchange 555-0100..555-0199. Personal e-mail runs
      on two invented consumer domains, `quillmail.com` and `brightpost.net`;
      work e-mail runs on the invented employer domains.
    reason: >
      Real free-mail domains cannot be used: the three commonest consumer
      mail domains are all on blocklist.txt as whole tokens (the corpus is
      full of them), so a synthetic packet carrying one would trip the Phase 5
      layer-3 halt. STYLE-SPEC §11 does not list them as shared house-style
      strings, so they would not be excused either. Invented domains cost
      nothing and scan clean. The 555-01xx block is the equivalent move for
      telephone numbers. Again the offending tokens are not quoted here — see
      decision D2's closing note.

  - id: D9
    title: "All names are rendered ASCII-only"
    decision: >
      `Siobhan`, not `Siobhán`. `Vu Thanh Ha`, not `Vũ Thanh Hà`.
      `Konstantinos`, not `Κωνσταντίνος`.
    reason: >
      The names travel through pypdf AcroForm values, a passport MRZ (which is
      A-Z, 0-9 and `<` only, with its own transliteration rules), Times New
      Roman docx runs and a `soffice --headless` conversion. Diacritics
      survive some of that and not all of it, and a mismatch between the MRZ
      transliteration and the printed name would break STYLE-SPEC §9.4's name
      lock for a reason that has nothing to do with the rule being taught.
      The input side may still show a client typing an accented name in prose;
      the packet is ASCII.

  - id: D10
    title: "T1's marriage predates her permanent residence by more than two years"
    decision: "Married 2020-03-14; LPR 2022-11-30; class of admission IR6; conditional_resident.was_cr = false."
    reason: >
      Had T1 become a permanent resident within two years of the marriage she
      would have been admitted as a CONDITIONAL resident (CR6) under INA 216,
      which produces an I-751 and puts C2 (Form I-797C) in play. Her mandated
      set is {C1, C3a, C3c, C4} = 10 documents, and a stray C2 would both
      break the target matrix and collapse her story into W2's — W2's
      conditional-residence history is W2's whole differentiator. Two years
      and eight months keeps her unconditional. Every client's
      `class_of_admission` is stated explicitly for the same reason: the green
      card exhibit prints the category and STYLE-SPEC §9.4 locks it.
      W2 is the ONLY conditional resident in the set (CR6, married 2022-02-19,
      resident 2022-09-15 — seven months, correctly conditional).

  - id: D11
    title: "Two clients carry family facts that trigger nothing"
    decision: >
      W3 Nowak is divorced and has a son; T3 Adeyemi is married to a
      non-citizen and has a daughter. Neither produces a single conditional
      document.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §9.3 rule 2 ("316(a) admits no spousal evidence at all") and
      §9.2 C3c (which requires `basis == 319(a)` AND a child AND a supplied
      passport) are both easy to mis-learn as "a spouse means a spouse's
      passport" and "a child means a child's passport". Two negative controls
      make the rule visible: T3 has a living spouse and no C1, W3 has a child
      and no C3c. Both are worked-or-tested against W2 and T1, where the same
      facts DO produce documents because the basis is 319(a). This costs two
      lines of masterkey and buys the rule its contrapositive.

  - id: D12
    title: "Both 319(a) clients file jointly, and DOCUMENT 6 absorbs the joint return"
    decision: "W2 and T1 file Married Filing Jointly; the joint return is DOCUMENT 6 and appears once."
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §16 ruling 13 and §9.3 rule 1. Stated at casting time because
      a masterkey writer with a joint return and a marriage-evidence cluster
      in front of them is one step from listing it twice, which would break
      the §4.4 lock (TOC line count == divider count == DOCUMENT count).

  - id: D13
    title: "T1's requested new name appears in exactly one place"
    decision: >
      Vu Thanh Ha requests the name `Ha Thanh Tran` on the N-400. That string
      appears ONLY in the Part 2 name-change item. The applicant cover page,
      the cover letter Re: block, the passport and its MRZ, the green card,
      the tax return and every other artefact carry the CURRENT legal name,
      `Vu Thanh Ha`.
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §9.4 locks surname and given name identical across the N-400,
      the passport MRZ and the cover letter. A requested name is a request,
      not a fact about any document that exists at filing. This is the single
      most likely fact error in the whole set and is repeated at the head of
      T1's brief.

  - id: D14
    title: "Nationality adjectives and their articles are frozen here, not derived downstream"
    decision: >
      "a Brazilian national" · "an Irish national" · "a Polish national" ·
      "a Vietnamese national" · "a Greek national" · "a Nigerian national".
    reason: >
      STYLE-SPEC §5's cover-letter template carries an `{A|AN}` slot next to a
      `{NATIONALITY ADJECTIVE}` slot. A renderer choosing the article from the
      first letter gets `an Irish` right and nothing else wrong here, but the
      rule is not "vowel letter" (it is vowel SOUND), so the article is stored
      as data alongside the adjective and never computed.

  - id: D15
    title: "Selective Service is No for every applicant, by construction"
    decision: >
      All three male applicants (W1 Almeida, T2 Stavros, T3 Adeyemi) first
      lived in the United States after their 26th birthday, so Part 9 Item
      22.a is No and 22.b/22.c do not arise.
    reason: >
      A `No` at 22.b is a real-world written-explanation trigger and would be
      a FOURTH C6 pathway competing with Item 20 — it would muddy the C5/C6
      truth table the set exists to teach. Arrival dates were cast to close
      it: Almeida first entered 2015 at 27, Adeyemi 2016 at 30, Stavros 2011
      at 54.

  - id: D16
    title: "Engagement dates run 5 to 9 weeks before filing"
    decision: "Each matter opens 5–9 weeks before it is filed; the input e-mail threads live in that window."
    reason: >
      Phase 4 writes threads dated between the engagement date and the filing
      date, and messes like 'password in a later e-mail', 'superseded address'
      and 'blank field supplied later by prose' need enough room for a
      chronology to exist. Under a fortnight there is no room; over three
      months the thread stops reading like one matter. Five to nine weeks also
      keeps every thread inside the 2025-11 .. 2026-07 in-world window.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# FIRM — §16 ruling 7. There is no firm identity in this build.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
firm:
  identity: none
  note: >
    STYLE-SPEC §16 ruling 7 (UPHELD AND EXTENDED) forbids a firm name, a
    preparer name, a business address, a firm telephone or a firm e-mail
    anywhere in any artefact — cover letter, signature block, N-400, or any
    other page. This registry invents none of them and nothing downstream may

from datetime import date

def add_years(d, y):

lpr = date(2022,11,30)

# marriage to LPR gap
gap_days = (lpr - marriage).days
print("marriage->LPR gap days:", gap_days, "=", gap_days/365.25, "years")

# residence years at filing

# engagement before filing

# travel window
window_start = filed - timedelta(days=3*365+1)  # approx 3 years back, using 3*365.25

EOF

def cd(s):
    weights = [7,3,1]
    vals = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch.isdigit():
            v = int(ch)
        elif ch == '<':
            v = 0
        elif ch.isalpha():
            v = ord(ch.upper()) - ord('A') + 10
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"bad char {ch!r}")
        vals.append(v)
    total = sum(v*weights[i%3] for i,v in enumerate(vals))
    return total % 10

content.content:
## 11. SHARED STRINGS — NOT LEAKAGE

Phase 5 layer 3 greps `lab/synthetic/blocklist.txt` against the synthetic tree
in both directions and allows zero hits. This section exists so that whoever
writes that scan knows the difference between a real hit and a string the house
style **requires** every packet to contain. All of the following appear in the
corpus *and* must appear in synthetic output; `build_blocklist.py` excludes
them by construction and they must never be re-added:

- The four lockbox blocks of §7 in both carrier variants — `USCIS`,
  `Chicago`, `Dallas`, `Elgin`, `Phoenix`, `Carol Stream`, `Tempe`,
  `Lewisville`, `P.O. Box 4380`, `P.O. Box 660060`, `P.O. Box 4060`,
  `P.O. Box 21251`, `131 S. Dearborn`, `2500 Westfield Drive`,
  `2108 E. Elliot Rd.`, `2501 S State Hwy 121 Business`, and their ZIPs.
- Agency and form vocabulary — `Department of Homeland Security`,
  `United States Citizenship and Immigration Services`, `N-400`, `I-551`,
  `I-751`, `I-797C`, `G-1450`, `1040`, `Form`, `Application for
  Naturalization`, `Permanent Resident Card`.
- Statutory citations and the fee — `INA`, `8 U.S.C. § 1430(a)`,
  `8 C.F.R. § 319.1`, `INA § 316(a)`, `8 C.F.R. § 316.2`, `316`, `319`, `760`.
- Every literal string frozen in §4 and §5 — `APPLICATION FOR NATURALIZATION`,
  `APPLICANT:`, `DOB:`, `COB/CON:`, `Classification Basis:`, `TAB A`,
  `SUMMARIES`, `TAB B`, `BIOGRAPHICAL`, `DOCUMENT`, `TABLE OF CONTENTS`,
  `Tab A (Summary)`, `Tab B (Biographical Information)`, `COVER LETTER`,
  `FORM N-400`, `PASSPORT`, `GREEN CARD`, `INCOME TAX RETURN`,
  `TRAVEL ADDENDUM`, `COURT RECORDS`, `VIA`, `Attn:`, `Re:`,
  `To Whom It May Concern:`, `Enclosed please find`, `Sincerely,`,
  `Petition Preparer`, and the two eligibility clauses.
- US state names and abbreviations, month names, country names, generic
  address nouns (`Street`, `Avenue`, `Apt`, `Suite`, `Floor`, `Box`).
- The vocabulary of the exhibits the build itself renders — 1040 line labels,
  deed and recorder terms, insurance-policy terms, I-797C notice terms, court
  disposition terms.

### 11.1 What the blocklist can and cannot see

`build_blocklist.py` harvests every `.txt` sidecar, every email body, every
`.md` report and every path name under `lab/`. **54 of the 185 corpus PDFs are
image-only scans whose sidecars are the stub `[NO TEXT LAYER — …]`** (FILE-MAP
§7), and every identifier that lives *only* on a scan — jacobs' A-number, zhu's
police case number, the deed and tax preparers — is invisible to that pass.

The script therefore runs a **second pass: `pdftoppm -r 200 -gray` plus
`tesseract` over each of the 54, cached by file hash in `tools/.ocr-cache/`**
so that reruns are offline and deterministic. OCR noise is *wanted* here: the
variant readings it produces are exactly the OCR variants FILE-MAP §7 says must
all go on the list ("Ma Lone" as well as "Malone"). Tokens read visually during
Phase 1 are additionally hardcoded in the script's `KEEP_ALWAYS`.

Two limits to carry forward. Tesseract's output is not pinned across versions,
so the *cache* — not the OCR — is what makes the build reproducible; delete it
and the token list may shift slightly. And OCR on a photographed card or a
hand-annotated court form is imperfect, so **the leakage scan is necessary but
not sufficient**. BUILD-PLAN §10 ranks leakage as risk 2 and puts the scan on
the never-cut list; this is a recorded hole in it, not a closed one. Phase 6's
final scan on the shipped tree inherits the same limit.

**Applicant-nationality exclusions are a casting constraint, not a blocklist
entry.** BUILD-PLAN §7 rules Australia, China, Mexico, the Philippines and
Italy out as *applicant* nationalities. Those country names still appear
legitimately in travel history, so they stay off `blocklist.txt`; Phase 2's
registry enforces the constraint instead.

---

## 12. FACTS THE OUTPUT CONSUMES

def cd(s):
    weights = [7,3,1]
    vals = {}
    for i,c in enumerate("0123456789"):
        vals[c] = i
    for i,c in enumerate("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ"):
        vals[c] = i+10
    vals['<'] = 0
    total = 0
    for i,c in enumerate(s):
        total += vals[c]*weights[i%3]
    return total % 10

def mrz_line1(surname, given_names, country="GRC"):
    line = "P<" + country + surname.upper() + "<<" + "<".join(given_names.upper().split())
    line = line.replace(" ", "<")
    line = (line + "<"*44)[:44]
    return line

def mrz_line2(passport_no, nationality, dob_yymmdd, sex, expiry_yymmdd, personal_no=""):
    passport_no = passport_no.upper()
    passport_field = (passport_no + "<"*9)[:9]
    pn_cd = cd(passport_field)
    dob_cd = cd(dob_yymmdd)
    exp_cd = cd(expiry_yymmdd)
    personal_field = (personal_no + "<"*14)[:14]
    pers_cd = cd(personal_field)
    line = passport_field + str(pn_cd) + nationality + dob_yymmdd + str(dob_cd) + sex + expiry_yymmdd + str(exp_cd) + personal_field + str(pers_cd)

    line = line + str(comp_cd)

digit_strings = set(re.findall(r'\b\d{6,}\b', text))

compact_ids = set(re.findall(r'\b[A-Z]{2,}[0-9]{5,}\b', text))  # e.g. MSC0918452207, PC7726154 etc.
proper_nouns = set(re.findall(r'\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z]{2,}(?:\s[A-Z][a-zA-Z]{2,}){0,4}\b', text))

    r = subprocess.run(['grep','-ixF', t, 'blocklist.txt'], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if r.stdout.strip():

print("HITS:", len(hits))
for h in hits:
    print(h)
print("checked:", len(candidates))
EOF

_notes:
  part_map_discrepancy: >
    n400-part-map.md (built from AcroForm /TU tooltips) claims the printed
    applicant-contact block is "Part 10" and the preparer block is "Part 12",
    with "no Part 13" on this edition. Direct `pdftotext -f 1 -l 12 -layout`
    extraction of the ACTUAL PRINTED PAGE TEXT of the committed
    lab/synthetic/blanks/n-400.pdf disagrees: the real printed sequence is
    Part 9 (Additional Information About You, items 1-37, pages 6-10) ->
    Part 10 (Request for a Fee Reduction, page 10-11) -> Part 11 (Applicant's
    Contact Information, Certification, and Signature, page 11) -> Part 12
    (Interpreter's Contact Information, page 12) -> Part 13 (Contact
    Information...of the Person Preparing this Application, page 12, WITH
    fillable fields — it exists and is not empty-by-construction).
    The underlying /TU tooltip TEXT is independently self-inconsistent (e.g.
    interpreter fields tagged "Part 11. Additional Information.. Interpreter's
    Contact Info", a page-10 checkbox tagged "Part 12. Additional Information
    About You") — it is stale in the same way n400-part-map.md already
    documented the field NAME prefixes to be stale, but the map's own
    prose table inherited the stale tooltip TEXT as if it were the printed
    label. This masterkey therefore identifies every N-400 block BY
    DESCRIPTION (per SPEC-DELTA D-H's own stated principle — "applied to the
    blocks the user named by description, not by number"), not by a Part
    number, everywhere it matters: `contact:` is the applicant's own
    phone/mobile/email block (filled), there is no `preparer:` key anywhere
    (empty, no firm identity), `contact.signature`/`signature_date` are null
    (unsigned). Field-level FILL/LEAVE-EMPTY behaviour still correctly comes
    from n400-part-map.md's AcroForm FIELD-NAME lists (P12_Line3_Telephone
    etc.), which are unambiguous regardless of which Part label is attached
    to them; only the prose Part-number labels are wrong, and only in that
    tool file, not in this masterkey. The task's own instruction to "key
    moral_character to the printed Part 9 items of THIS edition" is VALIDATED
    by this same extraction: Part 9 truly is items 1-37, and Item 20/Items
    15.a-b are exactly where both the task and registry.yaml say they are.
  part6_children_discrepancy: >
    The task's "WHAT THE MASTERKEY MUST CARRY" list states "Daphne is his
    child in N-400 Part 6". Direct extraction of the printed Part 6 shows
    Item 1 asks only for "your total number of children UNDER 18 years of
    age" and Item 2 limits the table to "children identified in Item Number
    1." Daphne is 42 at filing. She is recorded here as a `family.children`
    fact (STYLE-SPEC §12.5 requires it) but is explicitly marked
    `on_part6_table: false` with the reasoning inline, so Phase 3's renderer
    does not mistakenly place an adult daughter in a printed-minors-only
    table. Part 6 Item 1 for this applicant = 0.
  item_8a_finding: >
    brief.md's over-delivery mess list includes "his Greek military
    discharge paper" among documents that "still agree with the masterkey."
    Printed Part 9 Item 8.a asks broadly: "Have you EVER served in, been a
    member of, assisted, or participated in any military or police unit?" —
    with no carve-out for compulsory service. Konstantinos, born 1957 in
    Greece, is exactly the demographic for Greek compulsory national
    conscription (near-universal for Greek men of his generation) and the
    brief's own document manifest puts a discharge paper in his hands.
    registry.yaml's per-client `moral_character` block instead states
    "all_other_items: No, except the oath answers, which are Yes" — silent
    on Item 8.a and 12. THIS IS A BRIEF/REGISTRY DISAGREEMENT, flagged
    loudly per instruction. Resolved in favor of brief.md (this client's
    designated authoritative source, and the source that actually puts the
    discharge document in the packet's input pile): q8a = Yes (routine,
    honorable, non-combat compulsory service, 1976-1978), q12 = Yes
    (ordinary conscript weapons/basic training, same service). Both route to
    Part 14 only, exactly like Item 20 — NEITHER creates a new exhibit,
    NEITHER is an arrest, so C5 still does not fire and the exhibit set is
    still exactly {C4, C6} = 8 documents. The written explanation (DOCUMENT
    8) carries all three non-tabulable Yeses (8.a, 12, 20) in one document.
    Left at registry's stated "No" for 8.a, the masterkey would directly
    contradict a document the client actually sent — precisely the
    "unlocatable/contradictory fact" class the task calls a
    challenge-breaking bug for this dogfooded client.
  mrz_arithmetic: >
    Computed in Python (ICAO 9303 weights 7,3,1 cyclic; digit value = itself,
    letter value = ord(c)-ord('A')+10, '<' = 0), not eyeballed:
      passport field "AL5729184" (padded to 9 with '<') -> check digit 7
      DOB field "570412" -> check digit 9
      expiry field "280219" -> check digit 4
      personal-number field (all '<', unused) -> check digit 0
      composite over [passport+cd, dob+cd, expiry+cd, personal+cd] -> check digit 0
    Line 1: "P<GRCSTAVROS<<KONSTANTINOS<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<" (44 chars)
    Line 2: "AL57291847GRC5704129M2802194<<<<<<<<<<<<<<00" (44 chars)
  leakage_scan: >
    Every newly invented proper noun and every digit-string of 6+ characters

      block is printed Part 10 and its preparer block is printed Part 12,

      (Additional Information About You) -> Part 10 (Request for a Fee
      Reduction) -> Part 11 (Applicant's Contact Information, Certification,
      and Signature) -> Part 12 (Interpreter's Contact Information,
      Certification, and Signature) -> Part 13 (Contact Information,
      Certification, and Signature of the Person Preparing this Application)
      -> Part 14 (Additional Information) -> Part 15 (Signature at Interview)
      -> Part 16 (Oath of Allegiance). The blank's own /TU tooltips are
      internally scrambled, not merely lagged by a fixed offset — e.g. field
      `P10_Line1_Citizen` (page 11) is tooltipped "Part 7. Marital History,"
      which is nowhere near page 11's actual content. brief.md's own language

      carries no printed-Part-number labels for the contact/preparer blocks
      (see identity.contact.n400_field_note) — it names the actual field IDs

      Writing a contested Part number into this file would buy nothing and
      risks baking in the wrong one.

      `render_n400.py` fills by field NAME, so rendering is unaffected. But
      n400-part-map.md's DESCRIPTIVE table is wrong and SPEC-DELTA D-H's
      claim that "the committed blank has no Part 13" is false — Part 13 IS
      the preparer block. Flagged for whoever owns Phase 3/5 tooling; not
      fixed here, per the instruction to touch exactly one file.

      and her pre-Scioto employment as 2020-06-01 to 2023-01-06. Both leave a
      short gap against other facts already fixed elsewhere: the address gap

      addresses AND gap-free employment.

    "tax_return": "tax_return",
    "resume": "resume",
    "evidence": "evidence",
}
CONTACT_ALIAS = {
    "daytime_telephone": "daytime_phone", "daytime_phone": "daytime_phone",
    "telephone": "daytime_phone",
    "mobile_telephone": "mobile_phone",  "mobile_phone": "mobile_phone",
    "mobile": "mobile_phone",
    "email": "email", "email_address": "email",
}

# --------------------------------------------------------- Part 9 item table
# Read off the PRINTED page text of the committed 01/20/25 blank
# (`pdftotext -f 6 -l 11 -layout`), never off the stale /TU tooltips.
#   arrest        -> STYLE-SPEC §9.2 C5, court records
#   part14        -> the form routes the explanation to Part 14, so its own
#                    table cannot carry it: §9.2 C6, written explanation
#   oath          -> Part 12 willingness answers; "Yes" here is NORMAL and must
#                    never be read as a moral-character disclosure
ITEM_CLASS = {
    "15a": "arrest", "15b": "arrest", "16": "arrest",
    "8a": "part14", "8b": "part14", "12": "part14", "20": "part14", "21": "part14",
    "30a": "part14", "30b": "part14",
    "31": "oath", "32": "oath", "34": "oath", "35": "oath", "36": "oath", "37": "oath",
}
ITEM_TEXT = {
    "8a":  "EVER served in, been a member of, assisted, or participated in any military or police unit",
    "8b":  "EVER served in, been a member of, assisted, or participated in any armed group",
    "12":  "EVER received any weapons training, paramilitary training, or other military-type training",
    "15a": "EVER committed, agreed to commit, asked someone else to commit, helped commit, or tried to commit a crime or offense",
    "15b": "EVER been arrested, cited, detained or confined by any law enforcement officer",
    "16":  "If you received a suspended sentence, were placed on probation, or were paroled, have you completed it",
    "20":  "EVER been placed in removal, rescission, or deportation proceedings",
    "21":  "EVER been removed or deported from the United States",
    "31":  "Do you support the Constitution and form of Government of the United States",
    "32":  "Do you understand the full Oath of Allegiance to the United States",
    "34":  "Are you willing to take the full Oath of Allegiance to the United States",
    "35":  "If the law requires it, are you willing to bear arms on behalf of the United States",
    "36":  "If the law requires it, are you willing to perform noncombatant services",
    "37":  "If the law requires it, are you willing to perform work of national importance",
}

def norm_item_key(k):
    """q_15b / q15b / Q_15_b -> 15b"""
    s = str(k).lower().replace("q", "", 1) if str(k).lower().startswith("q") else str(k).lower()
    return re.sub(r"[^0-9a-z]", "", s)

def is_yes(v):
    a = v.get("answer") if isinstance(v, dict) else v
    return str(a).strip().lower() in ("yes", "y", "true")

def unwrap_list(slug, key, val):
    if val is None: return []
    if isinstance(val, list): return val
    if isinstance(val, dict):
        for cand in LIST_UNWRAP.get(key, []) + ["list"]:
            if isinstance(val.get(cand), list):
                return val[cand]
        # a dict-of-dicts used as a list (almeida's consistency_locks)
        if all(isinstance(v, (dict, str)) for v in val.values()):
            out = []
            for k, v in val.items():
                out.append({"lock": k, **v} if isinstance(v, dict) else {"lock": k, "detail": v})
            return out
    problem(slug, f"cannot unwrap {key!r} (type {type(val).__name__}) — add an alias")
    return []

def sidecar(slug, key, val):
    """Everything in a wrapper dict that is NOT the list itself."""
    if not isinstance(val, dict): return {}
    inner = set(LIST_UNWRAP.get(key, [])) | {"list"}
    return {k: v for k, v in val.items() if k not in inner}

def normalise(slug, k):
    n = {}
    n["client"]   = k.get("client", slug)
    n["slug"]     = slug
    n["ships_as"] = k.get("ships_as")
    for passthru in ("identity", "immigration", "family", "matter", "input_surfaces",
                     "documents", "derived", "correspondent", "fee_reduction"):
        if passthru in k: n[passthru] = k[passthru]

    # --- lists -------------------------------------------------------------
    for key in ("exhibits", "travel", "addresses", "employment",
                "mess_events", "consistency_locks"):
        raw = k.get(key)
        n[key] = unwrap_list(slug, key, raw)
        side = sidecar(slug, key, raw)
        # agents also parked metadata in siblings like travel_meta / exhibit_notes
        for extra in (f"{key}_meta", f"{key[:-1]}_notes", f"{key}_notes"):
            if isinstance(k.get(extra), dict): side = {**side, **k[extra]}
        if side: n[f"{key}_derived"] = side

    # --- contact -----------------------------------------------------------
    c = dict(k.get("contact") or {})
    for alt in ("identity", "matter"):
        for kk, vv in (k.get(alt) or {}).items():
            if kk in CONTACT_ALIAS and kk not in c: c[kk] = vv
    n["contact"] = {CONTACT_ALIAS.get(kk, kk): vv for kk, vv in c.items()}
    for req in ("daytime_phone", "mobile_phone", "email"):
        if not n["contact"].get(req):
            problem(slug, f"contact.{req} missing — printed Part 11 items 3/4/5 need it")

    # --- documents ---------------------------------------------------------
    docs = {}
    for kk, vv in (k.get("documents") or {}).items():
        docs[DOC_ALIAS.get(kk, kk)] = vv
    n["documents"] = docs
    if "applicant_passport" not in docs:
        problem(slug, "documents has no applicant passport under any known alias")

    # --- moral character ---------------------------------------------------
    mc, raw_mc = {}, k.get("moral_character") or {}
    if not isinstance(raw_mc, dict):
        problem(slug, "moral_character is not a mapping")
        raw_mc = {}
    for kk, vv in raw_mc.items():
        item = norm_item_key(kk)
        if not re.match(r"^\d", item): continue
        v = dict(vv) if isinstance(vv, dict) else {"answer": vv}
        v["item"] = item
        v["classification"] = ITEM_CLASS.get(item, "standard")
        if item in ITEM_TEXT: v.setdefault("text", ITEM_TEXT[item])
        mc[f"q{item}"] = v
    n["moral_character"] = mc

    # --- the derived booleans the exhibit rule actually needs --------------
    arrests = sorted(i for i, v in ((v["item"], v) for v in mc.values())
                     if v["classification"] == "arrest" and is_yes(v))
    part14  = sorted(i for i, v in ((v["item"], v) for v in mc.values())
                     if v["classification"] == "part14" and is_yes(v))
    oath_no = sorted(i for i, v in ((v["item"], v) for v in mc.values())
                     if v["classification"] == "oath" and not is_yes(v))
    trips = n["travel"]
    on_form = [t for t in trips if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("on_form") is True]
    trimmed = [t for t in trips if isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("on_form") is False]
    cr  = (k.get("immigration") or {}).get("conditional_resident") or {}
    basis = str((k.get("immigration") or {}).get("basis", "")).lower()
    spousal = "319" in basis
    in_hand = cr.get("unconditional_card_in_hand_at_filing")
    if in_hand is None:                       # kavanagh expressed it by dates
        in_hand = not bool(cr.get("was_cr")) or bool(cr.get("i751_approved_before_filing"))
    ev = {str(e.get("type", "")).lower() for e in (n["documents"].get("evidence") or [])
          if isinstance(e, dict)}
    n["rule_inputs"] = {
        "basis": "319a" if spousal else "316a",
        "was_cr": bool(cr.get("was_cr")),
        "unconditional_card_in_hand_at_filing": bool(in_hand),
        "arrest_items_yes": arrests,
        "part14_items_yes": part14,
        "oath_items_not_yes": oath_no,
        "trip_count": len(trips),
        "trips_on_form": len(on_form),
        "trips_trimmed": len(trimmed),
        "part8_rows": 6,
        "evidence_types": sorted(ev),
        "c1_fires": spousal,
        "c2_fires": bool(spousal and cr.get("was_cr") and not in_hand),
        "c3a_fires": bool(spousal and any("deed" in t for t in ev)),
        "c3b_fires": bool(spousal and any(("policy" in t or "auto" in t or "insur" in t) for t in ev)),
        "c3c_fires": bool(spousal and any("child" in t for t in ev)),
        "c4_fires": bool(len(trips) > 6 or len(on_form) > 6 or trimmed),
        "c5_fires": bool(arrests),
        "c6_fires": bool(part14),
    }
    if oath_no:
        problem(slug, f"oath items not Yes: {oath_no} — check before shipping")
    for extra in ("self_check", "_notes", "n400_numbering_note", "disagreements",
                  "leakage", "exhibit_notes", "signature_policy"):
        if extra in k: n.setdefault("_authored_notes", {})[extra] = k[extra]
    return n

def main():
    slugs = sorted(os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(p))
                   for p in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "clients", "*", "masterkey.yaml")))
    if len(slugs) != 6:
        print(f"expected 6 masterkeys, found {len(slugs)}: {slugs}", file=sys.stderr)
    shapes = {}
    for slug in slugs:
        src = os.path.join(ROOT, "clients", slug, "masterkey.yaml")
        try:
            k = yaml.safe_load(open(src))
        except Exception as e:
            problem(slug, f"does not parse: {e}"); continue
        n = normalise(slug, k)
        dst = os.path.join(ROOT, "clients", slug, "masterkey.norm.yaml")
        with open(dst, "w") as fh:
            fh.write("# GENERATED by tools/normalize_masterkeys.py — do not hand-edit.\n"
                     "# Edit clients/%s/masterkey.yaml and re-run.\n"
                     "# Everything from Phase 3 onward reads THIS file, never the raw one.\n\n" % slug)
            yaml.safe_dump(n, fh, sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True, width=100, default_flow_style=False)
        shapes[slug] = {kk: (f"list[{len(vv)}]" if isinstance(vv, list)
                             else f"dict[{len(vv)}]" if isinstance(vv, dict) else type(vv).__name__)
                        for kk, vv in n.items()}
        r = n["rule_inputs"]
        fires = [c.upper()[:-6] for c in ("c1_fires","c2_fires","c3a_fires","c3b_fires",
                                          "c3c_fires","c4_fires","c5_fires","c6_fires") if r[c]]
        print(f"{slug:16} {r['basis']}  exhibits={len(n['exhibits']):2}  trips={r['trip_count']:2} "
              f"on_form={r['trips_on_form']}  fires={','.join(fires) or '-'}")

    # prove one shape
    ref = None
    for slug, sh in shapes.items():
        if ref is None: ref, refslug = sh, slug; continue
        diff = {kk for kk in set(ref) | set(sh)
                if ref.get(kk, "-").split("[")[0] != sh.get(kk, "-").split("[")[0]}
        diff -= {"derived", "correspondent", "fee_reduction", "_authored_notes",
                 "exhibits_derived", "travel_derived", "addresses_derived",
                 "employment_derived", "mess_events_derived", "consistency_locks_derived"}
        if diff: problem(slug, f"container types still differ from {refslug} on: {sorted(diff)}")

    print()
    if PROBLEMS:
        print("\n".join("[problem] " + p for p in PROBLEMS))
        print(f"\n=== NORMALISE: {len(shapes)} written, {len(PROBLEMS)} problem(s) ===")
        sys.exit(1)
    print(f"=== NORMALISE GREEN: {len(shapes)} masterkeys, one shape, 0 problems ===")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
PY

**D-I — the six masterkeys are normalised to one shape before Phase 3 reads
them.** The six Phase 2b agents wrote correct content
in six different shapes:\n`exhibits` was a bare list in two and `{list: [...]}` in four (and adeyem
i\ninverted the field meanings, writing `{doc: <int>, id: <catalog id>}` where
\neveryone else wrote `{doc: <catalog id>, seq: <int>}`); `travel` appeared as a\nlist, a `{list:}`, a `{trips:}` and a `{countable_trips:}`; mo

ral-character keys
were `q1` in three and `q_1` in three; `documents.passport` was
`applicant_passport` in one; `tax_return.year` was `tax_year` in three.

`tools/
normalize_masterkeys.py` writes `clients/<slug>/masterkey.norm.yaml`, and\n**everything from Phase 3 onward reads only the `.norm.yaml`.** The authored file

stays as provenance. This is deliberately a normalise-to-disk step rather than an
import-time shim: with ~10 renderers, two verifiers, six Phase 4 fabricators, six
Phase 5
reviewers and three dogfood solvers still to come, a shim only works if\nevery one of them remembers to use it, and the failure when
one does not is\nsilent — a missing `on_form` flag reads as `None`, C4 quietly stops firing, the\nTOC comes out one line short, and the verifier

recomputes from the same raw file
and agrees. Normalising once, loudly, in one place, removes that whole class.

The normaliser also em
its `rule_inputs`, a flat block of the booleans STYLE-SPEC\n§9's four-argument rule actually consumes (`c1_fires`
… `c6_fires`, the arrest\nand Part-14 item lists, trip counts, supplied-evidence types). `verify_client.py`\nand `
validate_masterkeys.py` read those rather than each re-deriving the rule\nwith their own heuristics — two independent derivations of one rule is how

a
verifier ends up agreeing with a renderer's shared mistake.

One real bug this surfaced, and one of my own: `tran_daniel` carries a jo
int auto\npolicy in `documents.evidence` with `supplied: false` — a deliberate negative\ncontrol, since T1 must exercise C3a and C
3c but *not* C3b. The first normaliser\nread the evidence *type* alone and fired C3b, which would have shipped an\neleventh document. §9.3
rule 3 is explicit that C3a–C3c are a function of\n*supplied* evidence; the flag is now honoured and `evidence_declined` is car

ried
so the verifier can assert the negative.

**D-J — the leakage scan matches on distinctiveness, and it is poison-tested.**
D-F set
the policy; this is the implementation. Grepping every masterkey string\nagainst `blocklist.txt` raw produced 162–535 \"hits\" per client
and not one was\nleakage: the list carries ~12,400 tokens harvested from all corpus prose,\nincluding `
Allegiance`, `Constitution`, `Company`, `Additional`, `Engineering`,\n`Circuit`, `Republic` and `seal`. A scan that red-lights every client on

every
run is a scan nobody reads.

Four filters, in order:
1. **Scan only invented-f
act paths** — names, addresses, employers, contact\n   details, document and case numbers. Not `moral_character.*.text` (that is the\n   print
ed form's own wording), not agent commentary, not `input_surfaces` or\n   `consistency_locks` (those are prose about the facts,
not the facts).\n2. **Excuse house-style vocabulary by construction** — every word occurring in\n   the three committed blank forms, in STYLE-SPEC §11

, or in
   `templates/document-catalog.yaml`.
3. **Excuse ordinary English** via `/usr/share/dict/words`, after stripping
   possessives and
splitting hyphens (which is what finally cleared\n   `Self-Prepared`). The discrimination was verified before being trusted: that\n   list contains `engine

ering`, `circuit`, `pharmacy`, `republic`, `district`
   and `seal`, and does **not** contain `Oliveira`, `Izaguirre`, `Zhu` or

4. **

Force-flag the corpus's own distinctive nouns** regardless of the
   dictionary, because `Malone` is an ordinary dictionary word and would
   otherwise be excused.

Whole field

values are additionally matched against the blocklist entire, so a
multi-word address leaks even when each word is innocuous.

ison-tested rather than assumed.** Injecting `Oliveira` as a\nsurname, `SYMPLE` as an employer and `26 Broadway Fl 8` as a street into a\nmasterkey turns the barrier red on
all three and names the exact paths; removing\nthem returns it to green. A leakage gate that has never been shown to f

ail on
real leakage is not evidence of anything.

**D-I — the six masterkeys are normalised to one shape before Phase 3 reads
them.** The six Phase 2b agents wrote correct content in six different shapes:
`exhibits` was a bare list in two and `{list: [...]}` in four (and adeyemi
inverted the field meanings, writing `{doc: <int>, id: <catalog id>}` where
everyone else wrote `{doc: <catalog id>, seq: <int>}`); `travel` appeared as a
list, a `{list:}`, a `{trips:}` and a `{countable_trips:}`; moral-character keys
were `q1` in three and `q_1` in three; `documents.passport` was
`applicant_passport` in one; `tax_return.year` was `tax_year` in three.

`tools/normalize_masterkeys.py` writes `clients/<slug>/masterkey.norm.yaml`, and
**everything from Phase 3 onward reads only the `.norm.yaml`.** The authored file
stays as provenance. This is deliberately a normalise-to-disk step rather than an
import-time shim: with ~10 renderers, two verifiers, six Phase 4 fabricators, six
Phase 5 reviewers and three dogfood solvers still to come, a shim only works if
every one of them remembers to use it, and the failure when one does not is
silent — a missing `on_form` flag reads as `None`, C4 quietly stops firing, the
TOC comes out one line short, and the verifier recomputes from the same raw file
and agrees. Normalising once, loudly, in one place, removes that whole class.

The normaliser also emits `rule_inputs`, a flat block of the booleans STYLE-SPEC
§9's four-argument rule actually consumes (`c1_fires` … `c6_fires`, the arrest
and Part-14 item lists, trip counts, supplied-evidence types). `verify_client.py`
and `validate_masterkeys.py` read those rather than each re-deriving the rule
with their own heuristics — two independent derivations of one rule is how a
verifier ends up agreeing with a renderer's shared mistake.

One real bug this surfaced, and one of my own: `tran_daniel` carries a joint auto
policy in `documents.evidence` with `supplied: false` — a deliberate negative
control, since T1 must exercise C3a and C3c but *not* C3b. The first normaliser
read the evidence *type* alone and fired C3b, which would have shipped an
eleventh document. §9.3 rule 3 is explicit that C3a–C3c are a function of
*supplied* evidence; the flag is now honoured and `evidence_declined` is carried
so the verifier can assert the negative.

**D-J — the leakage scan matches on distinctiveness, and it is poison-tested.**
D-F set the policy; this is the implementation. Grepping every masterkey string
against `blocklist.txt` raw produced 162–535 "hits" per client and not one was
leakage: the list carries ~12,400 tokens harvested from all corpus prose,
including `Allegiance`, `Constitution`, `Company`, `Additional`, `Engineering`,
`Circuit`, `Republic` and `seal`. A scan that red-lights every client on every
run is a scan nobody reads.

Four filters, in order:
1. **Scan only invented-fact paths** — names, addresses, employers, contact
   details, document and case numbers. Not `moral_character.*.text` (that is the
   printed form's own wording), not agent commentary, not `input_surfaces` or
   `consistency_locks` (those are prose about the facts, not the facts).
2. **Excuse house-style vocabulary by construction** — every word occurring in
   the three committed blank forms, in STYLE-SPEC §11, or in
   `templates/document-catalog.yaml`.
3. **Excuse ordinary English** via `/usr/share/dict/words`, after stripping
   possessives and splitting hyphens (which is what finally cleared
   `Self-Prepared`). The discrimination was verified before being trusted: that
   list contains `engineering`, `circuit`, `pharmacy`, `republic`, `district`
   and `seal`, and does **not** contain `Oliveira`, `Izaguirre`, `Zhu` or
   `Symple`.
4. **Force-flag the corpus's own distinctive nouns** regardless of the
   dictionary, because `Malone` is an ordinary dictionary word and would
   otherwise be excused.

Whole field values are additionally matched against the blocklist entire, so a
multi-word address leaks even when each word is innocuous.

**The scan is poison-tested rather than assumed.** Injecting `Oliveira` as a
surname, `SYMPLE` as an employer and `26 Broadway Fl 8` as a street into a
masterkey turns the barrier red on all three and names the exact paths; removing
them returns it to green. A leakage gate that has never been shown to fail on
real leakage is not evidence of anything.

The §11 exclusion set this required is recorded, not hidden, in
`tools/blocklist-exclusions.txt` — `blocklist.txt` itself is not regenerated
because the run order forbids the OCR pass. Two masterkey agents independently
flagged `Self-Prepared`, and the `tran_daniel` agent flagged county and
court-type nouns, noting that T1 is the first client to carry a deed and no
worked pair has one. Both are in the file with their provenance.

**D-K — the tax-year rule in the first validator draft was inverted, and the six
agents were right.** It computed "filed before mid-April → previous year". The
correct reading of §13 D11 is that "latest tax return" means the latest return
that *exists* at the filing date, and TY N is not filed until roughly 15 April of
year N+1. So a packet filed before mid-April of year Y has **TY(Y−2)** as its
latest, and one filed on or after has TY(Y−1). All six masterkeys already had it
right; the validator was corrected to match them.
MD
